If he weren't so stubborn, we could be on our way home, already... But until then, I'll just have to show him that his little prank doesn't bother me at all!

entries.name: Chasing A-Me 01
entries.how:
Unfortunately, something's happened to one of my greatest inventions. You've seen mechanical squirrels, yes? Well, to get closer to the apes of Un'Goro Crater, I created a mechanical ape to blend in with their kind--I call her A-Me 01.

She has scrying gems for eyes so I could see everything she saw. She made it to Fungal Rock--the apes' lair--just east of here, and that's when I lost contact. The last thing I saw was one of their alpha males rushing up to say hello to her!

Can you help me find her?

entries.name: Chasing A-Me 01
entries.how:
A little further investigation shows a panel that slides open. Clearly written above some wiring is the statement, "Replace Mithril Casing And Turn Power Off Then On."

Taking a moment to replace the panel, you wonder if it'll be that simple to fix A-Me 01 and get her back to Karna Remtravel near Marshall's Refuge.

Only trying it will tell.

entries.name: Chasing A-Me 01
entries.how:
Checking to see if your prepared to lead A-Me 01 back to Karna Remtravel, you flip the switch to the "Off" position. Glancing around once again to make sure none of the gorillas are coming, you prepare to see what happens when you flip the switch back to the "On" position.

This is your last chance... are you sure this is what you want to do?

entries.name: Crystals of Power
entries.how:
I'm sure you've noticed 'em, {name}. They're everywhere!

What am I talking about? Why, the crystals, of course!

The crystals... They're all over the crater. Most people ignore them, but I have a strange feeling that they hold power within them. I've been doing experiments here with them for a while, but I can't seem to find anything. Well, I haven't yet, anyway.

Say, I'm running a little low on the crystals I have here -- think you might be able to collect some more for me?

entries.name: The Northern Pylon
entries.how:
What could they be for? I can't get the thought out of my head!

It's driving me crazy --  that the rumors I have heard about the crystal pylons are all true. Call me gullible, but I'll usually believe anything people tell me.

Anyway, I have heard that there is one of the crystal pylons fairly close. Somewhere in the north... Please locate it, {name}. I just know they exist.

entries.name: The Eastern Pylon
entries.how:
During my stay here, I have heard strange rumors about mysterious pylons existing out in the wilderness of the crater, {name}. I guess that they are quite large, with crystals lining their interiors.

Although I've never seen one, I can't help but think that the rumors are true -- and that the pylons have something to do with all the crystals we found

So why don't you help me put my curiosity to rest? Supposedly, there is one in the eastern area of the crater. Do you think you can find it?

entries.name: The Western Pylon
entries.how:
My experiments so far have not yielded any positive results, {name}. I can't help but hope that you can find a solution by searching for one of the pylons that I have heard exist.

Perhaps if we combine certain colors at them... but I get ahead of myself. Let's find them first!

{name}, search the western area of the crater; a pylon is said to be somewhere in that area.

entries.name: The Apes of Un'Goro
entries.how:
This crater has many strange creatures--they seem to be nobler versions of the creatures found throughout my homeland and beyond. I cannot explain it, but this place cries of the Earth Mother. I pay homage to her every time I track one of her beautiful creatures across its basin.

If you too wish to feel the enlightenment that accompanies such a great feat, then head to the north. There you'll find great apes who are a test for any mortal's strength. Bring me their pelts... prove your strength.

entries.name: The Fare of Lar'korwi
entries.how:
Once, a long time ago, a brother of mine took some meat from one of Lar'korwi's kills. He didn't know it at the time, but Lar'korwi saw him from the forest. Lar'korwi followed my brother for days, destroying everything he touched. My brother, scared, finally decided to run from the Crater and leave Lar'korwi behind.

Lar'korwi killed him not far from this spot.

If you want to provoke Lar'korwi, find a fresh kill of his and take some of the meat from it.

Return to me afterwards.

entries.name: The Scent of Lar'korwi
entries.how:
I'm actually surprised he has not come for you yet, {name}. But all is well, for I have a final plan that will bring the monster to us.

Being the dominant male gives Lar'korwi rights to breed with any female he chooses--and he chooses many of them. You'll find many ravasaur eggs to the west of here. Get close to them and you should provoke an attack by his mates. The females produce an awful smell from a gland in their heads that allow males to know they are ready to breed. Bring me two of those glands.

entries.name: The Bait for Lar'korwi
entries.how: This will be the most difficult part because there is some complexity to the plan. To the north of here, you will find a small trail into the mountains. It was here I saw Lar'korwi last. You will know you are in the right area because of all the bones from massive creatures that once wandered nearby. Take the meat you recovered and place it there. Then, rub this mixture I created on the meat. If both lures mingled together do not bring Lar'korwi to you, then I know nothing else that will.

entries.name: The Mighty U'cha
entries.how:
While you have been exploring Un'Goro, I have seen other things that a mighty hunter such as yourself would relish in. One such sight was a huge ape among the other gorillas to the north. You have been to that cave before, but this time, I wonder if you'll survive the encounter if you accept my task.

I call him U'cha, and he is one of the Earth Mother's greatest sons, of that you can be sure. Defeat U'cha and bring me his pelt. Do this, and I will defend your right to call yourself a great hunter.

entries.name: Making Sense of It
entries.how:
The information you have given me about the pylons is very interesting...

Give me a moment to do some calculations, {name}. Speak to me again in a moment and I should be able to give you the answer we have been looking for.

entries.name: Crystal Restore
entries.how:
The Pylon table allows you to combine green power crystals with yellow power crystals.

According to J.D.'s manual, this combination can be used to heal yourself or your allies.

entries.name: Crystal Force
entries.how:
The Pylon table allows you to combine green power crystals with blue power crystals.

According to J.D.'s manual, this combination can be used to increase your spirit.

entries.name: Crystal Ward
entries.how:
The Pylon table allows you to combine green power crystals with red power crystals.

According to J.D.'s manual, this combination can be used to strengthen the protection you have against physical damage.

entries.name: Crystal Yield
entries.how:
The Pylon table allows you to combine red power crystals with blue power crystals.

According to J.D.'s manual, this combination can be used to weaken an enemy's defenses.

entries.name: Crystal Charge
entries.how:
The Pylon table allows you to combine red power crystals with yellow power crystals.

According to J.D.'s manual, this combination can be used to create a large explosion that can inflict damage on your enemies.

entries.name: Crystal Spire
entries.how:
The Pylon table allows you to combine blue power crystals with yellow power crystals.

According to J.D.'s manual, this combination can be used to create a shield that does damage to enemies.

entries.name: A Little Help From My Friends
entries.how:
Ugh... It's so hot...

I was exploring this area, when all of a sudden, the heat just became unbearable. I must be suffering from heat exhaustion.

Please, help me get back to my friend Spraggle at Marshal's Refuge. I think I'm well enough to follow you there.

I am feeling a little out of it, so if I do happen to faint again, just splash some water on me from Spraggle's canteen. That should work, I hope...

entries.name: Lost!
entries.how:
You've got to help me, {name}! My friend, Ringo left earlier to explore the volcano to the south of here, and he has been gone way too long. I am really worried about him.

Do you think you could find him? Why don't you take my canteen with you -- if you do find Ringo, I'm sure he'll need it!

entries.name: Beware of Pterrordax
entries.how:
Wanted: A skilled fighter to deal with the threat of the Pterrordax that inhabit the Un'Goro Crater. Their numbers are growing, and they are becoming a menace to travelers in the area.

Decrease the population by slaying 10 pterrordax and 15 frenzied pterrordax.

Speak with Spraggle Frock after completing the task for a reward.

entries.name: Volcanic Activity
entries.how:
Being an apprentice to Marvon Rivetseeker, I've learned so much. But he's been gone for such a long time now, so I think I'm going to work on some experiments of my own.

I've been reading about Un'Goro Crater most recently, and about the strange volcanic activity going on in the middle of the crater. I think a lot could be learned if I could just get some of the ash from the elementals there.

Do you think you'd mind collecting some for me, if you are going that way?

entries.name: Shizzle's Flyer
entries.how:
I'm making a flying machine!

I got stranded here, and I'm absolutely horrible at finding my way around. I'd take a gryphon or wind rider back to Gadgetzan, but those beasts just scare me to death.

So, will you help me? All I have left to build is the wings, and I was thinking that the webby scales from the pterrordax and diemetradon would be perfect. There's no way I'm going to go up against one of those, but you look pretty tough. Why don't you give it a try?

entries.name: Dadanga is Hungry!
entries.how:
Dadanga looks up at you as you approach her. She seems to be hoping for something...

She's probably hungry!

There's got to be something growing in the crater that would be just the perfect snack for a large herbivore. Dadanga's a big girl; whatever you bring her, there would need to be a lot of it!

entries.name: Require Gnomish Problems
entries.how:
Ok bad news. This Gnomish consultant they got is one step ahead of me. Turns out their racer isn't even going to be on the ground! 

They are lining the racetrack with this thing called "magnets," and they are going to glide just above the ground, which means no explosion! If they won't step on the mine, then we just go to bring the mine to them!

I think if we have an electrical charge big enough, it should fix our issue. Go to Southwest Un'Goro and bring me a Thunderstomp Stegodon horn!

entries.name: Require Goblin Problems
entries.how:
Can you hear the explosions on the racetrack? No seriously, can you? Most of my hearing is gone. Anyways...

Magnets! By carefully placing magnets all along the racetrack and adding the reverse polarity to the bottom of our vehicle, we shall simply float above the mines! Take that Goblins! 

The last piece of the puzzle, we need something that can hold an electrical charge to manage the complicated electrical paneling. 

Head to Southwest Un'Goro and bring me a Thunderstomp Stegodon Horn!

entries.name: Haze of Evil
entries.how:
To tell you the truth, {name}, I've never seen any plants like this in my travels. Perhaps I should take a trip to this crater...

At any rate, I think I know just the thing Muigin's looking for -- Atal'ai haze. It's horrid stuff, hard to collect, but it's just what he needs to control the little monsters.

You'll need to visit the temple of Atal'Hakkar in the Swamp of Sorrows. The Atal'ai Haze can be collected from the deep lurkers, murk worms, or oozes found there. Good luck, {name}!

entries.name: Zapper Fuel
entries.how:
You're in luck, {name}! I've been working on some of my own experiments while Marvon's been gone, and one of them is a short range bug zapper. With just a few adjustments, it should be great for ridding yourself of those Bloodpetal pests.

I can let you have one of my zapper prototypes, but you'll still need to collect the fuel. You can get the necessary Atal'ai haze that the zapper needs in the temple of Atal'Hakkar. The deep lurkers, murk worms, or oozes are the ones you'll need to get it from.

entries.name: Uncanny Crystal
entries.how:
You may have seen some of the unusual crystal growths that dot this crater. I'm not a miner, but these growths don't seem to fit with the kinds of soil deposits all around here.

I believe I caught sight of a damaged crystal not far from here while I was foraging. I wonder if it holds any secrets about the origins of these strange formations? If you happen to spot it, I would love to investigate a sample piece.

entries.name: Microcrystal Contamination
entries.how:
This scale is slightly more reflective and iridescent than the others, as if it's embedded with tiny particles of crystal.

Torwa Pathfinder might be able to make something of this.

entries.name: Hol'anyee's Big Book of Big Lizards
entries.how:
I've been taking notes and making drawings in my sketchbooks of all of the creatures living in Un'Goro Crater, and I made a few copies so that I can send them to people who might be interested!

I have a sketchbook copy here that I've been meaning to get into the hands of the druids on Mount Hyjal, since I know that they love to study the natural world.

Hyjal's a bit of a trip, though. Do you think you could take it along in case you go there?

entries.name: Ravasaur Provisions
entries.how:
The Ravasaur in Un'Goro are entirely carnivorous. That means they only eat meat. This place may be chock full of resources, but that just means the jungle can turn into a bloodbath on the rare occasion when prey becomes scarce.

All across Un'Goro, you are going to find diemetradons and pterrodaxes. Bring me their meats!

entries.name: Silithid Intrusion
entries.how:
Though Un'Goro's ecosystem is stable and would survive all but a crashing meteor, there is one encroaching danger that threatens everyone and everything in the crater: the Silithid.

All it takes is one stray bug to start a hive, and sure enough, you can find ruptured ground leading into slithering tunnels along the southern mountains.

These creatures are vicious, and they spread like a plague. They're too close to the ravasaur grounds and must be culled.

entries.name: Stomping Giants
entries.how:
You might have heard of kodos, but have you heard of the stegodons? The kodo are descended from the mighty stegodons, but except for in the deep crater, the stegodon are gone! Far to the southwest, you will find a place known as Terror Run, the last place where this mighty beast still roams free.

They are a nuisance, and while more likely to be prey than predators, their enormous size and thunderous stomps deter most dinos from leaving their nesting grounds.

Kill a few, just to quiet things down.

entries.name: Wasteland
entries.how:
West of Un'Goro Crater, via the northwestern ridge, is a harsh wasteland - Silithus.  Few know that an ancient war was waged there between the night elves and a malign, alien power.  The evil was sealed, but now we suspect that forces work to stir this... unspeakable horror.

Seek out Layo Starstrike, one of our agents in Silithus; look for him at Valor's Rest, the final resting spot for the fallen of the wastes.  Give him this letter, and he will give you his trust accordingly.

entries.name: Shards of the Felvine
entries.how:
Your knowledge of Eldre'Thalas - Dire Maul - in Feralas will now come into play, {name}.  In the eastern part of the ruined city is where Alzzin the Wildshaper has exerted his corrupt dominion.  Go there with all due haste and brave whatever challenges await you.

The Fruit of Fertility, now corrupted as the Felvine, should be close to Alzzin.  When he falls, capture whatever essence of the Felvine you can.  Seal it in the Reliquary, and bring it to me.

Good luck, and Cenarion's speed.

entries.name: A Reliquary of Purity
entries.how:
The first step is to find a container capable of holding an extremely corruptible substance without the handler suffering ill effects.  There is only one sort device I am aware of that could possibly contain something as vile as the Felvine: a Reliquary of Purity.

Deep in the wasteland of Silithus is the remnants of the night elf village known as Southwind.  I know one was there many, many years ago.  If we are to succeed, I need you to scour those ruins in the hopes of reclaiming it.

entries.name: Uncovering Past Secrets
entries.how:
Anyway, you should check back with me relatively soon... that is if you want to know what was in here.  As soon as I find out what it is, and if it's indeed a book, I'd be happy to share that information with you.

In the meantime, I'd check in with the den mother of this little bear camp, Rabine.  No doubt he'll want to know what crazy antics you've been up to.  Never leave the den mother waiting, {name}... that is, unless you want to be doused in honey.

It's happened, trust me.

entries.name: The Nightmare's Corruption
entries.how: You must travel to the four dream portals of Azeroth. From each you must draw a fragment of the Nightmare's corruption. The dragonkin that inhabit these areas will hold such fragments. Return to me when you have gathered these fragments.

entries.name: The Nightmare Manifests
entries.how:
We must use restraint against Eranikus. We are to redeem him not destroy him.

Tyrande is already en route to assist us in this task. We must weather the dragon's blows and save Nighthaven from certain destruction.

Be on guard! You and your allies are our only hope.

entries.name: The Champion Returns
entries.how: The keeper awaits your return, {name}. Take the green scepter shard to Anachronos at the Caverns of Time.

entries.name: The Lost Saplings
entries.how:
In times of unrest, seeds may take root in bitter soil. Ancients born this way are prone to corruption. They wander hostile lands; never finding peace.

I have sensed four saplings who may be spared such a fate. They are lost among the Eastern Kingdoms, with leaves like that of each season.

Please, take this water to them, so that they may be healed.

Be warned, the water's magic is delicate. Teleportation will destroy it. Its potency will also fade over time.

entries.name: Return to Moonglade
entries.how: Return to Loganaar and inform him of what we've learned. I'm going to try and scout the temple myself to hopefully make contact with the dragons, or at least glean more information.

entries.name: A Fortuitous Turn of Events
entries.how: Well hello {name}! I was just standing here taking in the scenery and I just couldn't help but overhear your predicament. Fortuitously, I think I can provide just what you need to help you with your little "evil devouring nightmare monster" problem.

entries.name: The Bad News...
entries.how: So, the good news is that a solution exists. The bad news is that getting what you need to be able to survive the dread is going to require a bit of effort. I know, its unfortunate that it's so hard to get good help these days. If this adventurer had managed to do the one simple thing I asked them to do in the first place, you'd be tucking in a hot meal and a cold ale at an inn somewhere, none the wiser about any of this right now.

entries.name: The Lost Vambraces
entries.how: You see, I'm a knight of some renown and I recently took it upon myself to rid the land of a particularly terrible evil making its home on a nearby island to the east. When I found the vile creature, a truly epic battle was met. We must have fought for hours until at last I sent the beast into full retreat, no doubt run off to succumb to its wounds. I was barely able to make it back to town myself before I collapsed in exhaustion. The vambraces must have slipped from my arm during the battle.

entries.name: The Nightmare Manifests
entries.how:
We must use restraint against Eranikus. We are to redeem him not destroy him.

Tyrande is already en route to assist us in this task. We must weather the dragon's blows and save Nighthaven from certain destruction.

Be on guard! You and your allies are our only hope.

entries.name: Aid from Moonglade
entries.how:
<Ketharas takes the branch and studies it. He begins to whisper a druidic incantation and the branch begins to glow brighter. The sickly green crystal begins to react as well, seeming to draw in the light surrounding it.>

The secrets this branch holds are regrettably beyond my ability to discern. But I do sense... something.

Take the branch and go to town of Nighthaven in Moonglade. Ask Dendrite Starblaze for assistance.

entries.name: Ancient Allies
entries.how:
{name}, I have little more to offer. If you mean to make the long trek up the mountain, you might do well to speak with some of its ancient caretakers.

Follow the road to the west. Look north, toward the foot of the mountain. You will eventually see an outpost, a remnant of the guardians that once roamed the slopes. There is an ancient there named Fraxinus. He and his friends can assist you.

entries.name: The Staff of the Mountain
entries.how:
With all of the ingredients you assembled I was able infuse the staff you recovered with a new magic. You should now be able to bring this to bear to counteract the magic of the Wild Gods that Ve'han has so brazenly stolen.

We will need to test it, however. Bring this to the druid known as Tiala Whitemane at the Summit of Eternity. She may be able to help.

entries.name: Disturbed Grave
entries.how:
<Someone, or something, has rummaged through the dirt, leaving fragments of bone scattered about. An oddly shaped indentation leads deeper into the cold, wet dirt.

Something within the area may have caused the disruption.>

entries.name: More Work?
entries.how:
Battles are often long and hard fought, led by those willing to stand against an imminent threat and look death in the face.

The truth is, many sacrifices were made, not just on the battlefield. We often overlook those who do their part to contribute.

Just yonder is a peasant by the name of... well come to think of it, I don't even know his name. What kind of person am I? He's kept us well-tended and nourished throughout our stay.

Could you speak with him? Let him know the job's done.

entries.name: Leather for Inclement Weather
entries.how:
Livin' out in da wild for five years done take a toll on our supplies. We had to make dis place from scratch! We could use your skills as a leatherworker.

I need to repair some of da tents and buildings, and patch up some armor. You bring me a pair of Rugged Armor Kits and a Cured Rugged Hide, I help you turn it into something special.

entries.name: Eyes of the Watchers
entries.how:
Just north of here lies the ruins of battles past. A dwindling scourge presence remains.

Though the mindless undead are a threat themselves, the watchers maintain a vigilant eye on those entering the area, making removal of the scourge threat even more difficult.

Remove the threat by taking from these watchers that which they value most.

entries.name: Itching for a Fixing
entries.how:
We've been stuck here for five years, and we've had to build everything from scratch! Do you know how much I've had to improvise just to do any engineering?

Hey, if you can help me out with some materials, I can make it worth your time! Build me a couple of Mithril Casings and a Mechanical Repair Kit so that I can fix up some stuff, and I'll show you a few things I've figured out.

entries.name: To the Summit of Eternity
entries.how:
You've managed to cut a swath through the undead that have kept us trapped here for so many years, and for that we can never repay you.

I have one more favor to ask, on behalf of us all. We know that there are druids at the summit. They protect Nordrassil and the Well of Eternity.

Why did they never come help us to escape?

For five years we have been trapped here. At last we have a glimmer of hope... but why didn't the druids come for us?

Let someone know that we're still alive!

entries.name: Open Season
entries.how:
Deadwood set on my pup and his sire. He stood fast, fought to the death as our guard. We must go home, but the way is dark and full of jaws.

Stay near, guard us well. I will lead, you will fend, and we will see den safe.

entries.name: Meet the Elders
entries.how:
Thank you for helping gather bear berries. Small steps build trust! With the aroma of berry resin on you, the Elders should be more welcoming of you. 

Go and speak with Elder Mistpaw and Elder Pinespeaker.

entries.name: Barkskin Breakout
entries.how:
<A matriarchal furbolg speaks to you from within the cage>

"Deadwood trap me and my cub in tough cage. Key hang on Deadwood Warden belt. You hunt them, take key, lift latch, set us free. Do this, and Barkskin know your heart true."

entries.name: Rub Some Dirt In It
entries.how:
I haven't seen a {race} like you in years!

Oh, I don't know what to do! My friend Fraxinus is sick, and I can't leave him alone!

Could you please fetch me some Untainted Soil from the uncorrupted land southeast of here? I can make some poultices that may help him to feel better.

entries.name: Leaves to Ligatures
entries.how:
Have you seen those nasty tainted shrubberies wandering around this valley?

Those plants are mean, but some of them are not entirely toxic. Their leaves can have medicinal purposes.

Would you be so kind as to fetch me some Verdant Leaves? You'll have to do a little pruning, of course.

entries.name: Bark Bite
entries.how:
With the ingredients you brought, I can make some simple medicine. This poultice should aid Fraxinus. He is old, you know, and he was badly burned during the wars. His bark hurts and his limbs ache. He is my best friend and I just want him to feel better!

Take this poultice and apply it liberally to all of the places where his bark is split and his sap is weeping.

entries.name: Flags of Our Forebears
entries.how:
We been stuck up here for years, always fighting against de Scourge, but we never lose hope. We fight to survive. We fight for da Horde. Da Alliance shares dis fight, but we never forget dat we still got history. Still got blood.

Far to da east, at Dae'gun, dere are Horde flags from da war. Da demons carry scraps and remains as trophies from da battle, especially da tough ones. Bring me a flag and some heraldry so I can put it up and show da Alliance dat da Horde is still strong!

entries.name: The Western Post
entries.how:
With the warlocks under control, I'd say this area's well in wing.

<The crow nods sagely, looking pleased.>

Though our work here is done, there are other areas that could use your help and as an underwing of mine I would like you to go see what all the fuss is about.

Follow the path northwest up the road to the old tern outpost. An old friend awaits!

entries.name: Spear of the Skylord
entries.how:
While fighting off the Wormwing harpies I was brutally ambushed by a harpy named Zarrat who patrols this area. She snatched my spear and carried it off before I could recover. To what end she desired to possess it, I cannot say.

That spear has been in my family for generations and is of great importance to me. If you spot Zarrat among the harpies, slay her and return my spear. She is stealthy, and will not be easily found, but I would be grateful to have my spear returned.

entries.name: Celastrus the Bitter
entries.how:
The mountain is overrun with wild growth, inflamed by the fel energies that rained down so long ago. Now the weeds and plants are angry, corrupted, poisoned.

There is a great thorn-bush called Celastrus that lurks about the slopes to the east. It kills animals, lashes out at other plants, feeds on the bodies of the dead. It must be destroyed!

The weeds must be cleared so that the mountain may regrow.

entries.name: Premiere Parts
entries.how:
Another new face? 

I shouldn't be surprised with the strength of our so-called wards these days. How's the fel down there? I haven't been away from this workshop in weeks. Say, while you're here, I do have some favors you may be able to help me with if you find yourself in the mood for errands.

You wouldn't believe how tricky it is to get proper parts all the way up here, let alone general building material for engineering. Nami in Everlook has a parts order waiting for me - care for a winter sprint?

entries.name: Crate Expectations
entries.how:
There's something you should know about this order. There's a few inverted mana cells padded as well as I could at the bottom of the box. The cells have a tendency to discharge when they get bumped, and when not stabilized in time. It takes about two hours for the contents to fizzle.

Kaylaena will know what to do when she receives them, but I suggest going slow if you're going to ride saddled up Mount Hyjal.

If you need a refill, come back and I'll top off the canisters. Be careful, you know?

entries.name: Rubble Rummage
entries.how:
I'm going to need some time to sort out which plans to build first. Something I've been meaning to do is hike up to the old Horde base and see what kind of treasure can be made out of whatever trash is laying around there.

If you are heading up there, and have the space to carry it, keep your eyes peeled for scrap metal, wire, or chunks of bat... droppings! Look, it has its uses okay!

You can find the remains of the horde encampment far up the mountain, even beyond the Elderwild settlement.

entries.name: Fox Hole
entries.how:
Every time I take my attention off the supplies I've lugged up here for more than a few minutes, one of nature's finest thieves is pilfering and rummaging through it.

The damned foxes seem to have made a burrow beneath the boulders nearby. Apparently, me digging out this hole gave them an idea of their own.

I'm working on a solution. Tell you what, bring back some of their fox tails. That'll teach them a lesson, and I'll hang the tails around the perimeter to scare the others off!

entries.name: Area Denial Skunks
entries.how:
You say you want to help? Alright, I've got a task for ya.

Ever been skunked on a hot day? Nothing worse, I tell you. Bloody things cover everything within spittin' distance in the most vile lingering stench!

A family of skunks have started making their home behind my equipment crates. Help me gently expel them from our perimeter and I'll think about sharing some of this gear, once we can get to it...

I can't stress this enough: don't attack them - they WILL spray you!

entries.name: Rootwork
entries.how:
The roots of Nordrassil stretch far and deep, thicker than riverbanks and older than memory. Such great size carries a great hunger. In healthy times, they drink of decay and renewal alike, drawing strength from the endless turning of the natural cycle.

But Hyjal has been wounded, its soil fouled by demonic venom.

Descend into the deepest depths of the Well of Eternity. Study the roots there closely. We must know whether they have drawn in too much corruption... or if the World Tree may yet endure.

entries.name: Cleansing Winds
entries.how:
The flying creatures of the Summit still draw breath from the highest currents, where the corruption has not yet fully taken hold. Hippogryph feathers and chimaera hair drift through these winds, absorbing what the air remembers of an unspoiled land. I need these remnants to anchor and strengthen my purifying incense.

Gather them for me, so I may concentrate the wind's knowledge into cleansing smoke before we begin the ritual.

entries.name: Tree Free
entries.how:
Let's try something else. You see that branch up there? Yep! That one. I need you to break it for me. I've got plenty of ropes tangled elsewhere, so there's no chance for catastrophic failure... I hope.

Take a safe step back and take a few swings at this branch, would you?

<Fenwick gestures at something above his head.>

Please be careful!

entries.name: Rocket Gnomes
entries.how:
My brother Fenwick and I recently finished a successful rocket test, the only problem is, he hasn't come back yet! I lost sight of him floating off to the south after his parachute deployed.

It looks like he may have landed in Hyjal!

If you help him find his way out of where he landed, I'm sure he'd find a way to thank you. I'll be grateful to have my brother back!

entries.name: Anywhere But Here
entries.how:
<A spirit materializes before you, recovering from a full-body yawn.>

You have no ranks with you... and you are not dressed as a soldier. We repelled Archimonde then?

It's been so long. I had almost forgotten what I once was, but you... you must be one of the first to walk these craters in years.

<The veteran glances at his surroundings.>

Let us continue our conversation at an overlook with a view I remember vividly, just west of here. Long ago, I left my scabbard to rest there.

entries.name: Lifted by Legacy
entries.how:
Hyjal is difficult to bear. Nightmares and murderous memories linger among the craters.

But you carry warmth from Kalimdor within you! My friend Tobin also enlisted and joined up with me, but I fear the worst for his soul. 

The Alliance company gave us steeds to break in and bond with for our upcoming deployment. We took them on a joy ride through the Barrens. Carved our names into the bottom of the Great Lift in Thousand Needles.

See if the marks remain? It will bring ease to a weary soul.

entries.name: Praise
entries.how:
Going so far out of your way solely for the fading wishes of a lost soul--thank you, {name}. The presence of a hand contemplating the carvings, with the fragments of history that you know so far, was enough to bring me here. My presence, now, is tied to the strongest bond with the still-living.

I beat Tobin to the salt flats, and he smoked me on the raceway. 

I recall clearer now. Meet me in Mourning's Rest--the site of our last battle--next to the broken cannon near the destroyed tower on the cliff.

entries.name: Of Friend and Fur
entries.how:
I see you try, and try is more than most. We give you good will with time, if you do the same.

Enter our den and talk to Osi. She has open paws, will give you more chance to help.

entries.name: Highfeather Helper
entries.how:
I am one of the last of the Highfeathers, the true followers of Aviana. We respect and revere the Matron of the Skies, and we call the Druids of the Talon our allies.

The Wormwing harpies have overrun much of this plateau. They reject our protector Aviana, and seek only to despoil the lands around us.

Blood has been spilled and must be repaid. Scatter their feathers to the wind.

entries.name: Paying Back the Pact
entries.how:
The Blackthorne Pact. That's what they call themselves. Apostate druids that have taken over Hyjal Summit. Violent, and extremist. They blame Malfurion Stormrage for robbing them of their immortality, and have sworn to reclaim the power that they were forced to relinquish. I did not understand the magic that empowered them before, but it's becoming clear now.

Take the staff, use it on the Blackthorne druids around the mountain. It should respond to and dispel the wards protecting them.

entries.name: Taking to New Heights
entries.how:
To defeat Ve'han,  we require a touch of the sky. A bit of the divine, where one's upward-turned face yearns to fly.

Head to the Shrine of Aviana and seek out Skylord Omnuron. As the leader of the Druids of the Talon, he can assist in adding a touch of Aviana's grace.

entries.name: Back to the Grind
entries.how:
Och, we had to make this village from scratch with what we could scrounge up after the war. All of the fighting has taken a toll on our weapons, not to mention the need for tools!

I can always tell another blacksmith. Think you could spare the time and materials to make me some Dense Sharpening and Dense Grinding Stones? We could really use 'em!

entries.name: Stolen Life
entries.how:
So, the hermit druid seeks a force to balance the 'life' in this magic of his? Then the answer is death, naturally. You have come to the right place for such a thing.

No doubt you've seen the undead crawling all over my domain. They are fueled by stolen power that animates them even in death.

That stolen power is exactly what is needed in this spell you speak of. Kill the undead and search through their skulls for a coalesced Drop of Stolen Life. Return it to Ketharas once you have it.

entries.name: Siegecraft
entries.how:
With the extra supplies you brought back, I have enough materials on hand to finish up Yaely's original plans for this Glaive Thrower. I've been fixing this thing up for the past... well, it feels like forever!

If you can help me out and be a second pair of hands, it'd make this whole project go a lot faster! I can walk you through it, most of the hard stuff should be out of the way... 

<Kaylaena crosses her fingers.>

The driving system and the energy cells powering it are nearly set up.

entries.name: Drum Up Trouble
entries.how:
There is a fel chimaera terrorizing beasts and travelers along hills. It is known to the Cenarion Circle as Ghansurok. I'll handle the aim and firing of the glaive thrower. Go to that drum by the cliff side. Let's see this blight driven from the mountain for good.

I'll only have a chance of shooting it down if you can draw its attention. Once you have the beast by the ridge, find some place to hide!

Yes, I promise I have a full bag of maple seeds!

entries.name: Ashes of the Legion Ascent
entries.how:
This magic you seek is as complex as it is wild. It needs a reagent that can provide a stable source of continual energy, and I know of just the thing.

When Archimonde met his well-deserved end here, many of his lesser minions were also killed. His chief lieutenant, Azgalor, was slain--by mortals like you, no less!

You'll find the last physical remains of Azgalor in the middle of the ruins here. No need to bring all of that ash back to Ketharas. Just a pinch should be more than enough for his needs.

entries.name: Now We're Cooking
entries.how:
Hey! I'm pretty busy trying to turn these scraps into something edible. You wanna help out? I could really use some more variety for this meal! It sure would be nice to have something different on the menu.

There's a goblin in Everlook who has this recipe for Savory Stag Sliders... perfect for tiny hands like mine. If you could cook up some of those, that would be great! You can get stag meat from the stags here on the mountain.

entries.name: Head Scratcher
entries.how:
South of here, among da forests where I sometimes hunt, dere is a great and cunning bear. We call him Head Scratcher, as his paws have caught more dan one unsuspecting villager. He ambushes hunters who are returning with prey, striking da heads by surprise and knocking dem unconscious, then stealing da catch and running back into da forest.

He is wise to me, he knows dat I track him. But he may not know your scent yet.

Take dis carcass and lure him out. Finish him and bring back his claws.

entries.name: Blight No More
entries.how:
Ever since we escaped the war we have struggled to secure our safety, surrounded by foes on all sides, beset by constant danger.

Our old holdout to the east is overrun with undead. These scourge meander mindlessly--a sad but dangerous remnant. Without the guidance of their commanders, they are lost... but still deadly.

Though we've tried, we have yet to succeed in eliminating their presence. At the very least, with your help, we can push them back to secure our safety... for now.

entries.name: A Bit of the Sky
entries.how:
Since the shrine of Aviana has fallen into disrepair, the Wormwing harpies have snuck in and stolen the last of our druidic relics. One of these, the Jewel of the Horizon, is a sparkling blue stone blessed by the feathered goddess herself. The touch of Aviana may have just the magical power that you need for your task.

The Wormwings have doubtless hidden it in or near one of their nests. When you find it, take it to Ketharas.

entries.name: The Demon Tower
entries.how:
You know I'm a warlock, right? Now reduced to squalor and meat-cutting, but once a mighty magician!

My imp keeps wandering off and while I could just call him back, I'm kinda curious about what he's doing. He's been sneaking off to talk to a bound satyr at a tower to the southeast of here. If you wouldn't mind, I'd like to know what they're talking about.

I'm sure it's nothing to worry about, but you can never tell with demons, right?

entries.name: Twisted Tools
entries.how:
I have worked iron my whole life, and I can feel when a weapon has twisted away from its purpose. The Blackthorne cult forges tools meant to wound the land as much as flesh. Slay their cultists and bring me what they carry: one of their staves, and a ritual dagger.

They do not merely kill with their blades, they are poisoning them with intent.

By studying the marks left by their corruption, we can learn how their influence spreads. Perhaps, we will learn how to stop or even reverse it.

entries.name: Ravenlock's Quest
entries.how:
You have performed your part well, {name}.

I have a quest of my own. There is a force here, demonic in nature. This otherworldly evil has permeated this mountain for an age. I have seen its corrupting influence reaching out like greedy black tendrils. As this evil sleeps, it dreams, and its dreams bring madness for any that its corruption may touch.

Come, step closer to the fire with me. We shall learn the name of this beast, and in so doing, obtain the means of its undoing.

entries.name: Final Death
entries.how:
We've tried to escape the mountain, but our attempts have always been thwarted by the Scourge. A powerful lich reanimates the remains of those we destroy and sends them against us again. So long as that lich endures, we'll never be safe.

The lich has a pile of bones from which it rebuilds skeletons. Take this torch and set fire to the bone pile in the ruins. The lich will be sure to respond.

Bring me its amulet, so that we may destroy it and be rid of the lich for good.

entries.name: Final Death
entries.how:
We've tried to get off da mountain, but da Scourge always stop us. A powerful lich reanimates da remains of da ones we destroy and sends dem against us again. Dat lich is da reason we can't win!

Da lich has a pile of bones dat it uses to rebuild skeletons. Take dis torch, go to da ruins, and burn da bone pile. Da lich be sure to respond.

Bring me its amulet, and we destroy it and get rid of it for good!

entries.name: Avalanche of Corruption
entries.how:
Well, you've shown you're capable enough to handle the busy work. Now we can see if you can be trusted to handle greater threats.

Setting up an intelligence station here is only step one of the job. If you want to help lay the foundations for what's to come, carefully enter Dae'gun, the remains of the Horde base.

Find a high point suitable for an outlook's post. Report back with details about the area, and we'll see about getting you properly briefed.

entries.name: Kindling, Kinda
entries.how:
While you're traveling around the mountain, I can't resist asking for another small favor...

Did you see all those fel shrubberies and plants littering the hills down below? It turns out they burn rather well, which is both good, and bad. Handy for feeding into a small furnace, but also a risk when it twists together and binds up gears...or bootstraps!

Thin their numbers on your way down, and I'll pick up the weeds myself once they've dried out.

entries.name: Feathers in Flight
entries.how:
We been tryin' ta leave many a time, but keep gettin' pulled back ta defend our brothas an' sistas. Wit our defenses dwindlin', it's time we get ta restockin'.

Today we be needin' arrows. Lots an' lots o' dem.

Find dem big, beautiful birds and bring us back dem long feathers for da straight shootin' arrows.

entries.name: Branch Out
entries.how:
<Fenwick struggles to rock back and forth and gain some swaying motion.>

Hey! Hey you! Grab a stick and see if you can reach me, please? I've been stuck here so long my suspenders are chafing! I've got good things--GREAT things--to share with you! Fenwick Togglespring never gives false promises!

It's my rusty brother back at the launch pad who clearly miscalculated a few things in our rocket launch capabilities! He's mister false promises!

<Fenwick fails to grab an object out of reach.>

entries.name: Ve'han's Fall
entries.how:
Ve'han now claims the Nordrassil Lodge, under the boughs of the great tree, as his lair. It is time for us to put this magic to the ultimate test.

Take the staff and bring it to bear against Ve'han. Dispel the magic protecting him and bring him to justice!

entries.name: The Dying Ancients
entries.how:
This corruption... seeps into my limbs, my roots. I am not the only one. Other ancients... have felt this corruption as well.

One of my oldest friends... Sunderbark... the corruption has broken him, made him a creature of rage and pain. It is... too late to save him, now.

Go to the corrupted pool to the east... strike the corrupted tree and he will come.

Take this seed... and plant it in his remains when the deed is done. With care... something good can still grow from this sorrow.

entries.name: Siphoned Ephemeral Essence
entries.how:
A lingering demon presence remains to the east. Among them are the hellish beasts responsible for ravaging our kin, siphoning their power to use it against our allies.

Penetrate their camp, locate these beasts and slay them. Retrieve any samples that remain.

Perhaps there is something we can learn from these efforts.

entries.name: Summit Sentries
entries.how:
The Wild King may have a numbers advantage, but we can outmaneuver him with tactics.

Empower our living sentinel stones across the encircling hills, they can track Blackthorne movements for us. The northern ridges, the southern slopes, and the western high ground all have drained stones that will activate upon detecting your allied presence.

Tread carefully as you work, Blackthorne patrols crowd these paths, and their presence is precisely why we must bring this land under vigilant surveillance.

entries.name: Mending Communications
entries.how:
With all of the fighting and the retreat from the Nordrassil Lodge, we've been terribly shorthanded out here.

If you are traveling back and forth between here and Everlook, I have some mail that needs to go to the town for distribution, and we need any waiting mail brought back up. I have a stack of parcels ready for transport, if you would be so good as to help.

entries.name: Top of the Post
entries.how:
Now that you've recovered all the mail, you can take it all back with you to Mount Hyjal!

Should be no problem, right?

entries.name: Contents Under Pressure
entries.how:
A sturdy backpack stuffed with survival equipment and radio receivers lies between prickly bushes. There's a flashing indicator light on one of the radios.

You reach for the bag and the radio strapped to the backpack buzzes to life.

"Pilot present! Gnomal Positioning System establishing uplink!

Confirming contents to dispense: Aviator's Survival Kit, Three Day, One Size, Quantity One

Please stand by while security mechanism discharges safely before opening."

entries.name: Unfrozen Deliveries
entries.how:
So you need to bring the return mail back to Mount Hyjal, eh? There's a little problem...

Y'see, someone came through here and ransacked the outgoing mail just a few days ago! Probably looking for money in the mail. Ran off into the hills somewhere north of here and never came back. Probably got torn apart by a yeti or something!

Anyway, if you wanna bring back the mail, you're gonna have to go get it first!

entries.name: A Thorn in the Paw
entries.how:
We need to improve our defenses here, and we lack the resources to construct fortifications. We do, however, have all of the bounty of nature.

Search the forest for thorn bushes and bring their seeds back to me. With the power of nature, we will grow our own defenses.

entries.name: Blackthorne Blackout
entries.how:
The Wild King listens through shadows older than Hyjal itself. His scouts move with purpose now, stirred by the renewed advances of both Horde and Alliance in these sacred lands. The Blackthorne Pact feels the pressure of our resistance and grows more crazed each day.

Hunt down the Blackthorne Courier and end her trail before she carries their important information back to her master.

She moves between camps. Watch her path, and strike her down. Bring what she carries back to us.

entries.name: Bait the Beast
entries.how:
The most vicious fel chimaera of Hyjal is known as Ghansurok. It likes to swoop in and prey on wildlife caught out of their burrows. Not only that, it's making hippogryph travel in and out of Hyjal more stressful than usual!

First, hunt down one of the Nightsabers hiding in the Summit's shadows. Next, place meat from the fallen cat somewhere on the northern ridge where chimaeras feed.

Lure Ghansurok towards it. Slay the beast and return with its heart. Marn will study it to help heal Hyjal.

entries.name: Wake Memories
entries.how:
It's a heavy thing to stand in Hyjal, where so many companions met their unnatural ends. The land itself echoes with grief. Craters filled with ash, memories too bitter to forget.

Yet you carry a spark from the Eastern Kingdoms, a warmth that defies this gloom! My childhood friend Tobin enlisted alongside me, and though I hold hope, I fear for what remains of his soul.

We'd spend afternoons skipping stones as kids across Lake Everstill in Redridge. Look for a shoreline anchor, and honor our pastime?

entries.name: Challenger of the Gods
entries.how:
Ve'han's research notes describe his attempts to steal the power of the Wild Gods, following the ambitions of his leader, the Wild King. His successes were few, and hapless. Had he been a more powerful druid, he likely would have quickly devoured the essence of Jereman and gained even more power still.

The Guardians of Hyjal at the summit camp will definitely want to know about this.

entries.name: A Thorny Solution
entries.how:
We are constantly under threat here, both by the Blackthorne Pact and by the hostile creatures of Hyjal. But we can use the thorns to our advantage! With a little help from the power of nature, we can grow new thorn bushes to help protect our enclosure.

Plant thorn seeds near the road to help create barricades by the inn, the storage tower, and the grouping of trees near the road.

entries.name: Praise
entries.how:
You went out of your way for the fading wishes of a lost soul--thank you, {name}. The sight of another spirit at the lake, thinking of two friends competing to see who can throw further--it's enough to draw me to this moment. Presence clings to the strongest bond with the living.

We never did skip a rock from one side to the other... 

<The ghost gazes across the lake.>

I recall. Meet me in Mourning's Rest--the site of our last battle--next to the broken cannon near the destroyed tower on the cliff.

entries.name: Ends Meet
entries.how:
This mountain cliff to the southeast... the remains of the tower. Seared into my mind, their harrowing screams still echo forever in memories.

Allow me to unburden myself and tell you of my defeat.

entries.name: Cult Closure
entries.how:
The lands surrounding the Well of Eternity are overrun with followers of the Wild King. Many once stood beside us, bound by the same oaths, but their devotion has curdled into reckless zeal. They actively hinder our efforts to tend Nordrassil and protect the Well.

I will not pretend this is easy, nor that my hands will be clean. Still, we cannot allow them to harm our land or strike our flank when the greater incursion begins.

Thin their ranks swiftly, and may Elune forgive what necessity demands.

entries.name: Kits and Cats
entries.how:
Oh, a tasty morsel...

Fear not, I jest. Though I could snap your spine like a dry branch. I am a demigod of the wilds, after all.

If you would gain my favor and avoid my appetite, perhaps I could burden you with a task?

My litter of young have wandered off to entertain themselves. Little on this mountain could threaten them directly, but there are dark things afoot near the summit, and I'd leave nothing to chance.

Would you check on them? In return for my not eating you, of course.

entries.name: Prey and Predator
entries.how:
The hierarchy of the Wild Gods is bent. Now, all is in motion, and the nature of the world is as malleable as clay!

No more will my kin suffer the fangs of predators, for now, we shall prey upon all who have devoured us!

Tremble, fragile creature, for you have neither the strength nor the speed to dissuade us!

entries.name: Violence Into Verdure
entries.how:
The old hulks of the war are decaying and rusting, but we can speed the process of reclamation.

Take this bag of the seeds that you collected before. I have given them a small helping of magic to speed their growth. Place them near the old war machinery and let them grow over and cover them. The memories of the war will fade into the past and nature will reclaim its space.

entries.name: The Bounty of Nature
entries.how:
You have done well and helped me, and the mountain, greatly.

I am just preparing some stew, and I would be glad to share it if you would help me gather some of the ingredients.

While I am loath to slay any among the wild animals, the cycle of life requires sustenance. A balance of ingredients would serve us well. A few Hyjal Venison Cuts from the Hyjal Stags would pair well with the starchy roots of the Scarlet Dart Tuber plants that grow in the green places nearby.

entries.name: The Pact
entries.how:
It seems that Ve'han has successfully stolen at least a portion of the power of a Wild God. Such a thing seems beyond belief to me, but here we are.

And what is this "Pact" Ve'han spoke of? {name}, you must return to Ketharas. Tell him what you've learned.

I'm sorry to say but it is likely well beyond your abilities to put a foe such as Ve'han down. Only the power of--well, the Wild Gods themselves may be able to counteract this magic.

entries.name: The Eyes of the Spire
entries.how:
This was once a helm of sorts, though it is difficult to tell it now in its twisted form. We can restore it, however. Like all things, there is a cost to this.

Go to the bastion of Blackrock Spire and claim the left eye of the false warchief, Rend Blackhand. From there, reach the pinnacle of the stronghold and claim the right eye of General Drakkisath, chief agent of the Lord of Blackrock.

Do this and you will remove two great evils from the world. Then I will cleanse the artifact you hold.

entries.name: Barkbound Blessings
entries.how:
You wish to learn from us? The trees of Hyjal speak to us. Their bark holds life, and on it grows the moss we call Moonveil. It is soft, green, and strong with the mountain's soul. We need this moss to heal our hurt and bless roots.

Go, gentle one. Seek the old trees where the mist clings and the sun hides. Take Moonveil moss from their bark and bring it back to me. With it, we will mend what pains us.

entries.name: Deal Dread to Deadwood
entries.how:
The old ways are lost to Deadwood. Their claws rip the wood, their hearts burn with rage. They strike at us, and the wilds shake.

You, friend of furbolg, can help. Go to their den. Show them the wild will not bow to greed. Slay those who foul the roots, and come back when their cries fade from the trees. Bring an end to their wise, but sad, sages. They twist fel and foul vines.

Do this, and we will speak to the spirits of your name.

entries.name: Windswept Wards
entries.how:
The mountain winds bring dark signs. Harpies nest high where our paws do not go. The gems they wear hold strong power. Bound with our charms, they guard us from curse and bind the spirits to our wards.

But the climb is hard, and the harpies strike with claw and storm. If you are strong like they say, go to the high crags where the wind screams. Harpy grounds are in mid land Hyjal, we see them fly above us, in the north east. Take the charms from the sky witches and bring them to me.

entries.name: Herbs of the Hollow
entries.how:
The mountain's breath is damp here by the spring, and my herbs will not dry in this thick air. When our kin return from the wild, they hang their packs wherever the roots allow good air, spread through the den.

Go now. Find the strands of dried herbs hung round our home and bring them to me. With them, I will weave wraps and wards to keep our spirits strong.

entries.name: Water of Hyjal
entries.how:
The Deadwood dwell by a pond born of Mount Hyjal's snow melt. That water is pure, strong with the mountain's breath. We use it for our draughts and to save roots from death.

Here, the springs run slow. Our source must be saved, and used with care. But their pond flows with life, it could fill our den twice over. Bring me a skin filled with that water, friend. Spirits will bless your steps, and our den will drink deep of the mountain's gift.

entries.name: Sweetpaw Jam
entries.how:
You smell like mountain winds, strong and free! I have a task, if your paws are not full.

We love bear berries, they're round, red, and sweet as honey after frost. Look for them near the shade of trees. Too many sharp rocks and mad wings for us to get the ripest bush.

Bring me a bunch, and I make Sweetpaw Jam! My best treat, and I will share a taste.

Deal?

entries.name: Shatter the Stonewatchers
entries.how:
High slopes hold stone wings. Rock-beasts. Half-live, half-dead. Foul hands carve them. Do not trust their still pose. These eyes wait for one wrong step.

Our young do not know the risk. One paw too near, and stone wakes with claw and fang.

Go, smash these cursed forms. Break their wings, crush their shards, and let the mountain breathe free.

entries.name: Wicked Wisdom
entries.how:
The owls of Hyjal are more than feathers and flight. Their talons, their plumes, even the bones whisper of the wild. We use these gifts to craft talismans, charms that bind the spirits and shield our kin.

But the owls do not give freely. You must take what the mountain offers. Kill oa owls and bring their carcasses to me.

Yes, we ask you to return the whole body to us, as we waste nothing provided by such graceful creatures.

entries.name: Burrow Beetles
entries.how:
Burrow beetles! They're a bane... and now they dig in our den more than their own. We beat them back and swing clubs when we see them skulk by, but they are quick, and to hide in the dark is their shield.

If you spot them as you climb our den, squash them! We will take their crushed shells and make a meal, so it is not all bad.

entries.name: Work Well Done
entries.how:
The magic that Ketharas was able to craft to counteract this threat was vital to this victory. Our druids should be able to replicate the magic and use it to dispel the wards empowering the Blackthorne Pact at scale.

You should go back to Ketharas and let him know what transpired here. Tell him that he has the thanks of the Guardians of Hyjal and the Cenarion Circle. He should know that he is always welcome amongst us should he desire a place alongside his fellow druids once again.

entries.name: Balance Through Strength
entries.how:
Barkskin stand on weak roots. Deadwood claw at our land, each day their rot digs deep, sinks more. We cannot hold alone. 

Deadwood Den guards are the brunt of their strength. If you seek our trust, strike down those who foul the wood. When their Guardians fall, the rest of their tribe will weaken. We even our odds.

Bring them down, for balance, and help keep Hyjal whole.

entries.name: One Person's Trash
entries.how:
Picking up the rusting metal, you see another, shinier, engineering component. It looks like anything else of use has been picked clean.

Perhaps somebody nearby recognizes this part or who might want to salvage it.

entries.name: Barkskin Beginnings
entries.how:
Some may speak with you now, but not all. For more of our tribe to be what you know as friend, you must not rush.

Stay by our side, work with our young and old, and guard us from those who wish us harm.

When you have more to bring to us, we will have more to share.

entries.name: The Western Post
entries.how:
With the warlocks under control, I'd say this area's well in wing.

<The crow nods sagely, looking pleased.>

Though our work here is done, there are other areas that could use your help and as an underwing of mine I would like you to go see what all the fuss is about.

Follow the path northwest up the road to the old outpost. An old friend awaits!

entries.name: Blight No More
entries.how:
Escapin' war don't mean we be safe here. Dem creatures to da east been plaguin' da area all dis time.

Maybe you be ready for a challenge, eh?

Strike 'em down. Ain't nobody gonna be missin' dem after all.

entries.name: Feathers in Flight
entries.how:
We always need more arrows for hunting and fighting, and for feathers, we use the white feathers of the Hyjal owl. They're naturally fluffy and soft, but I stiffen them up with a mixture designed to make them perfect for fletching.

You can get feathers from the owls, of course, but they also leave behind feathers in their nests, which you can find all over to the south of here.

Bring back a bundle of feathers, all right?

entries.name: Deeproar Down
entries.how:
One chief of the Deadwood, Deeproar, barks in the depths of their den. He was once of no burrow, and in a night of bad blood, he fell sway to their spells.

Now, he feeds on their sour sap, with twice the cursed roar.

Go. End his foul ways. Take his staff and bring it here, so I know he holds it no more.

entries.name: Mystic Mix
entries.how:
With far sight, we have seen their den. Deadwood brew dark rites in their pots. They feed this foul mix to their young, so bad roots take. Then they learn to fight with vile ways.

Go, stop this spread. Slay the dark ones and smash their stew.

entries.name: More of the Same
entries.how:
The Light has forsaken me. A purpose served, and now everything... gone...

It's just a matter of time until the light turns to darkness.

I fought against the demons and scourge forces with a ferocity I did not know the Light could produce... and yet, I sit here, talking to you, feeling... well, I can't quite put it into words. Some reclaim their purpose after loss, yet I struggle... After all, I am only who I am.

Now, unless the commander has one last call to action, I await what comes next.

entries.name: To the Summit of Eternity
entries.how:
You cut down so many of da Scourge dat we finally have a little safety. For dat, we be thankful.

One more thing. We know dat there are druids at da summit. Dey protect da great tree and da well.

How come dey never helped us?

We been here five years! Why did dey never even send a message to anyone about us? Let someone know dat we still here, we still alive!

entries.name: Water of Hyjal
entries.how:
Now that we know Deadwood don't foul the water outright with their presence, we can take this sample and cast our wards with sound will. We've heard there is a pool of the mountain's tears within their den.

Travel with force and pour this water into the pool deep in Deadwood Den. 

Return to us when you have learned what secrets the dark depths hold.

entries.name: The Experimental Method
entries.how:
Alright dirtwalker, you may have noticed the combination of pinecones and fel-infused slime is quite disgusting, if you ask me. It is, however, also very dangerous-- which is just what we need!

Take these pinecones and carefully--I repeat, carefully--make your way to the nearby warlock encampment. Once there, use these items to wreak havoc upon their precious workstations.

I am sure the results will be amusing for you to watch firsthand! This should certainly slow them down.

entries.name: Notation, Notation, Notation
entries.how:
Listen, {class}. There have been some awfully noisy visitors just up the mountain. They are tainting the land with their foul demon magic and experimenting with piles of ash. It's high time we investigate.

By we, I mean you.

I want you to poke around and investigate their camp! See if you can bring me some notes on what our mysterious fel 'friends' have been up to. Surely with egos that large they've written something we can utilize. Perhaps they are carrying something on their person?

entries.name: Taste of Ash
entries.how:
So in order to really disrupt operations here and get me out of this cage, we're going to have to kill four very powerful mortals. This cage has demonic wards on it that won't be dispelled until all four are dead, and that key can't be used until the wards are down.

Look, you seem like a {race} that can hold your own but I'm going to need a bit more convincing that you can actually take on these stupid warlocks before I give you any good info.

Like killing a ton of these warlocks for starters. Easy, no?

entries.name: Crystalline Collection
entries.how:
Listen, I know you can smell the fel blood pools behind me and I'm sure you've seen the crystals that grow out of them. These crystals have special properties from the ashes of Archimonde that rain down on this side of the hill.

Something about how they are formed makes them especially good at draining fel energies, which is a big problem for someone like me, but they can still have their uses.

I want you to gather some for me. Try and get a few kinds. I'll know what I need when I see it.

entries.name: A Curious Question
entries.how:
There is a caged demon just up the road near the entrance of the demon caster encampment that has been making a great deal of fuss.

All this ranting and raving about imprisonment and freedom. Something about scorching bones and revenge?

<The crow leans in and gives you a mischievous look. As if to emphasize, she then dangles an iron key in one of her talons.>

Let's see if we can't make a deal with our little 'friend' and see what he knows about these nasty demon casters.

entries.name: The Hydra's Head
entries.how:
It is time to cut off the heads of this hydra, if you catch my meaning.

There are three leaders who need to be killed in order to slow the operations here. Conveniently, they also need to be slain to remove the wards on my cage.

Tyaeha can be found in the House of Diseases by the creepy tree. Dazka is in the Alchemist ward with all the potions, and that fool Frezzlie is undoubtedly next to the slime pits along the northern ridge of the encampment.

Go slay them and bring me their bones!

entries.name: A Revenge So Sweet
entries.how:
Brashann Grimdark, Master of Vessels.

<Felflick's mouth curls into a snarl.>

He was the one to subjugate me at the summit. HE is the reason I am here in the first place.

His work with these fel-ash crystals are the backbone of this operation. He's been obsessively experimenting with anchoring souls in these crystals and his work has not gone unnoticed by those Blackthorne creeps.

Use this pristine crystal to drain his power, then put an end to him and bring me his soulstone.

entries.name: A Prolific Source
entries.how:
Listen here, {class}. It seems we're in quite the sticky situation. I knew those blasted demon casters were up to no good, but this is far worse than I had expected.

Good thing I have an idea!

For this to work I will need fel-slime from the surrounding slime creatures that can be found in the fel blood pools behind me. Not the bones or bits, just the slime! Make sure you wipe your hands after handling it. It seems to be corrosive.

Not to fear, I'm sure you'll find a way to bring it back to me.

entries.name: Seeds for a New Season
entries.how:
You have arrived on Mount Hyjal at a time of changes, stranger.

You may have seen that the landscape is scarred by the old war and tainted by fel energies. For Hyjal to survive, nature must bloom again.

If you are willing to help me gather seeds from some of the untainted plants, I would be grateful. Many flowers grow in the wild lands east of here. Look for small red or yellow flowers.

entries.name: Hope for Hatchlings
entries.how:
The owls are under threat by the fel corruption that afflicts the mountainside, and the creatures poisoned and enraged by those energies. Many owls have abandoned their nests for safer places higher up the mountain. Others have fallen in defense of their young.

For the owls to have a future, their eggs must be protected and their fledglings nurtured. Bring the abandoned eggs to me. You may find eggs in abandoned nests at the base of trees north and east of here.

entries.name: Rites of Respect
entries.how:
One cannot take without giving in return. This is the cycle of life.

You have done well, {name}. Thanks to your efforts, the wildlife on the mountain will continue to thrive.

Now, it is time we show our respect for these lands by offering the unused remains back to the ground.

Take this bundle and visit the shrine to the west. You shall recognize it as a simple pair of standing stones. Return to me once the ritual is complete.

entries.name: Fine Feathered Friend
entries.how:
The cycle of renewal has finally begun. The ancients... shall rise again, and the power of the natural world take its course... to bloom.

You... have helped us tip the scales in nature's favor. Perhaps... we can yet make a larger impact... on a more dire situation.

Head west... where the land itself is ashen... and you may find an entity who can help. She may look like just a small bird... but her power is great.

entries.name: Threading a Solution
entries.how:
Every day be a challenge when you living rough like we do! Takes a toll on your tools, your clothes, your whole life. Good thing it can't take our spirit!

We be really hurting from our clothes and blankets wearing out. You do some tailoring, right? So maybe you can bring me some Bolts of Runecloth and I can fix a few holes?

entries.name: Stemming the Demon Tide
entries.how:
Ah, a {class}. I see great strength and determination in you--qualities necessary to rid these lands of evil.

The demons that walked these lands during the great battle were defeated, yet some still remain. It is important to prevent them from escaping.

The ruins to the east are dangerous. Carry your strength into their den. Destroy the unwelcome before our lands perish.

entries.name: Drawing Down the Malevolent
entries.how:
As suspected, the vessels fused into something new--something powerful.

I suppose if the vessels capture stored energy, there must be a way to use that power to our advantage. Fel artifacts are rarely safe or easy to come by, but we might as well do something with it, hmm?

Time for a field test.

Take the crystal and use it against Bethra'zel and Mazzogore--two of their most powerful demons. Their presence alone has ensured the camp is well protected. Let's see if we can change that.

entries.name: As the Crow Flies
entries.how:
Thank you for your help, {name}. A dear friend of mine awaits your arrival at the summit.

You can find her up the road to the east.

entries.name: Belle's Ring
entries.how:
Yes, Thomas Belle.

<Daythor's demeanor changes suddenly, appearing as though to recall a fond memory of this individual.>

Thomas was one of the first to fall as the scourge laid siege to our outpost. I hadn't heard of his passing until the battle was over. Tragic... He was such a promising young man.

I suppose it would be right for us to deliver this to his beloved Michelle. If memory serves me right, he spoke often of Goldshire.

entries.name: An Oldstone But An Old Friend
entries.how:
I'm sure you've met that old stick-in-the-mud, that lives in the cave south of here? 

You must take this staff to him along with my feather. He will know what it means. Or he won't! Either way it will get his attention.

He may be an oldstone, but he is reliable. He's one of the few mortals I would trust with a matter as grave as this. 
 
Quickly, Dirtwalker! I fear a shadow is falling over Hyjal we cannot see.

entries.name: Past Wing and Claw
entries.how:
Traveler, be wary! Though the Shrine of Aviana lies ahead, the area is claimed now by the harpies of the Wormwing tribe.

Like my family, the Highfeathers, I am a follower of Aviana, but the Wormwings are not so loyal. They are a danger to anyone who passes through their territory.

If you can make your way past them, my cousin Phoebe Highfeather helps to protect the shrine.

entries.name: Tarnished Treasures
entries.how:
{class}, I would ask a favor of you. One that is deeply personal.

When they ambushed and killed my sisters, the Wormwings took their jewelry claiming these treasures as trophies of battle. What's worse, they've stashed our treasures in their nests with their unborn young; further proof of their depravity.

Please collect my fallen sisters' treasures. Avoid harming the unhatched eggs if you can, but I'll lose no sleep over the broken eggs of our enemies.

entries.name: Amalgamated Marrow
entries.how: <Something wriggles ominously within the bone pile as green ooze seeps out from under the freshly added bones.>

entries.name: Prickly Pinecones
entries.how:
I've known these hills since I was a hatchling. If there is one thing I know, it's that pinecones can solve a lot of problems.

Probably not what you expected, eh?

<The crow winks at you, conspiratorially.>

Go fetch me some; it's part of a little scheme I'm hatching. I promise you it will be worth the effort.

You should be able to find them under any healthy or living tree nearby. Stay away from those corrupted ones though, those pinecones aren't any good!

entries.name: Fetid Corruption
entries.how:
<The second you near the pulsing nodule it falls from the tree, exposing a weeping green sap. It seems the tree has corruption within its bark that has spread deep, but the tree is not yet dead.

Looking around it is clear it has spread to some of the surrounding trees, but not all suffer from the same level of corruption.

Perhaps it is not too late to save the infected trees nearby.

Surely the Highfeathers would be grateful if you remove as many corrupted knots as you can find.>

entries.name: Power Wash
entries.how:
With the venomous, poisonous heart of the chimaera Ghansurok in hand, soak in the ancient waters of the Well of Eternity.

Watch closely how the waters react to the corruption, how nature remembers what systemic corruption has tried to unmake.

Bring the organ back to me, and together we will read the signs it bears, and learn whether balance can yet be restored... or if the wound runs too deep.

entries.name: Arch Absolution
entries.how:
I've compacted this potent, pungent resin. Take this prepared incense and stand before the fallen form of The Defiler's remains.

Speak the incantation as the smoke rises, not to banish what remains, but to steady the spirit. His visage still carries the memory of terror, and even now it stirs fear in those who linger too long.

Let the smoke carry calm and resolve, warding the mind against dread, so that those who walk this place may remember the victory, not the horror.

entries.name: Memory Mist
entries.how:
{name}, the ancestral spirits called to Hyjal during the great battle weren't all lost. Some linger still, drawn to Nordrassil after the great sacrifice. These wisps have stayed within the root canopy that hangs over the well, trapped in a state of purgatory between this world and the next.

Use this enchanted branch to bring peace to these wisps, joining their memories with eternity.

You need not release them all yourself. Recover the will of five and return the branch to us.

entries.name: The Dying God
entries.how:
I... don't have much time, mortal. You must take this staff, a branch of the world tree... corrupted... wrong. I carried it here...

The Wild Gods... they must know. Take it to her. The... crow...

<The dying Wild God grows still and his eyes stare blankly ahead. What little is left of his corporeal form seems to break apart and drift away. There is a faintly glowing branch on the ground, with a sickly green crystal affixed to its head.>

entries.name: A Revenge Now Bitter
entries.how:
You know, for a mortal I'm impressed with how easily you follow orders.

You just went in there and killed all of those people without batting an eye!

Ahhhh... but now it's time for YOUR end of the deal, 'friend'. I've helped you dismantle the moronic Ashen Reign, take out their leaders and cripple their operations here.

I think I've earned my freedom.

<Felflick's eyes glimmer in anticipation.>

entries.name: Skill Issue
entries.how:
Have you had the opportunity to speak with Aisarra yet? I would assume the conversation has been fairly one-sided if so. As someone trained in keeping secrets, she prefers to stand watch rather than engage in pleasantries.

She is looking for someone with a mastery of a variety of trade skills, and your name was mentioned as someone she had hoped to mentor.

Unfortunately I don't think your skills are quite up to her standards, but I think you two may get along if you practiced a little more.

entries.name: Honorable Mentions
entries.how:
You continue to prove yourself a worthy ally of Hyjal.

I would like to share more of my knowledge with you. This time, I believe you have earned the right to choose your destiny. Of the remaining patterns I am willing to share for this particular endeavor, you may pick to specialize in either shoulders, gloves, or boots. As before, I will offer one of your choosing for free.

Whatever armor you choose to forgo today, I may still be willing to teach you later.

entries.name: A Crafter's Reverence
entries.how:
The master craftsman returns. Your presence is welcome.

By now, I assume you need no reminder of the details of our agreement, but I will offer a refresher nonetheless. From the options that remain, you can choose one more type of armor to focus your skills on. Additionally, I will offer another recipe from my selection to you for free.

Of the final type of equipment that we pass over today, you will be able to learn after more victories.

entries.name: A Fitting End
entries.how:
<Felflick cackles gleefully as he regards the bloody bones of the Ashen Reign leaders.>

Oh this is just perfect!

<Felflick hops back and forth in his cage, snickering all the while.>

Now it is time to give those warlocks the fate they deserve. There is a massive bone pile to the west of here if you follow the road. Trust me, it's impossible to miss. That's where all their 'failed' experiments go.

That is where I wish to dump these fools' remains. Let the whole world know what failures they are!

entries.name: Gathering Storm
entries.how:
With the perimeter scouted, you've proven useful and trustworthy enough to bring into the fold.

I'm here representing SI:7's efforts to gain crucial information important to the Alliance. Not just anyone is privy to this knowledge. Mind your discretion.
