entries.name: Scrying Goggles? No Problem!
entries.how:
<You hear a sigh of relief escape the crate.>

You just want his scrying goggles? Great! That will be no problem... Just give me a minute to... Hey! Where the... Dagnabbit!

Well, there's some bad news and some worse news. The bad news is that I lost the goggles. The worse news is that I lost them when I was nosing around in the Molten Core last month. Yep, the Molten Core... I guess that concludes our business! Bye!

entries.name: Remember Alterac Valley!
entries.how:
Make no mistake about it, {name}.  The Horde is quite right when they say Alterac Valley is Frostwolf Territory.

You see, the Stormpike Expedition arrived as peaceful visitors to the area in search of ore and relics.  The Frostwolves reacted with the most brutal and uncivilized act of aggression the Alliance has experienced.

Let us never forget the brave dwarves that perished in that cowardly unannounced attack.  Go now, {class}, do your part in the battle for Alterac Valley.  For the Alliance!

entries.name: Remember Alterac Valley!
entries.how: The Battle in Alterac Valley rages on, {name}!  Have you done your part as of late, {name}?

entries.name: Invaders of Alterac Valley
entries.how: The battle for Alterac rages on!  You must return to Alterac Valley and once more drive the invaders out of Frostwolf territory, {name}!

entries.name: Brawl at the Maul
entries.how:
There must be more to the Maul than this!

Perhaps the loud Spectator who oversees the event at Dire Maul will know!

entries.name: Brawl at the Maul
entries.how:
There must be more to the Maul than this!

Perhaps the loud Spectator who oversees the event at Dire Maul will know!

entries.name: Brawl at the Maul
entries.how:
There must be more to the Maul than this!

Perhaps the loud Spectator who oversees the event at Dire Maul will know!

entries.name: Vanquish the Invaders!
entries.how:
Beyond this tunnel you will find a field of strife and turmoil, young {class}. The Horde continue to decimate our sacred forest, cutting down the evergreen foliage to power their machines of war.

Enter Warsong Gulch and defend Silverwing Hold. Push back the invading Horde forces!

Do this, and earn a talisman of merit.  Bring me such a talisman, {name}, and I shall reward you.

entries.name: Quell the Silverwing Usurpers
entries.how:
The wilds of the Ashenvale forest will succumb to the might of the Horde, {race}. Nothing the Silverwing say or do can stop our sovereign imperative. Kalimdor belongs to the Horde. How dare they attempt to prevent us from harvesting what is rightfully ours!

Let the pride swell in your chest as you cut down their weak attempts at slowing our progress. Destroy the Silverwing Sentinels, and earn a Warsong mark of honor.  Return to me with such a mark, {name}, and you will be rewarded.

entries.name: Ribbons of Sacrifice
entries.how:
I understand that it can be difficult at times to come out on top in Warsong Gulch.  Still, your effort on our behalf - even when victory is not achieved - is important.

Should you complete one of the trials inside Warsong Gulch and not achieve victory, you will still receive a Ribbons of Sacrifice.  Bring it to me so that the Sentinels may reward you for acting on our behalf... even if you weren't able to win this time.

entries.name: Battle of Warsong Gulch
entries.how:
The battle in Warsong Gulch against the Silverwing Sentinels is of great importance.  Under the guise of protecting a forest that doesn't belong to them, the Alliance seeks to deny the Horde one of our largest sources for lumber.

Do not let this happen, {name}!  Come back to me with proof of serving the Horde in a worthy manner!

entries.name: Fight for Warsong Gulch
entries.how:
The Silverwing Sentinels are at war with the Warsong Outriders due to the destruction the Orcs are causing to the forest.  There are, however, more reasons to defend this particular forest than plain love for nature.

The forest forms a strategic barrier that makes Ashenvale defendable against a large-scale attack.  Without it, Astranaar would last a day or two before being annexed to the Barrens.

Do your part in fighting the Warsong Outriders, {name}!  For the Alliance!

entries.name: Fight for Warsong Gulch
entries.how: Don't forget the fight for Warsong Gulch is about more than just protecting trees.  It's about keeping a natural barrier between Ashenvale and the Barrens.  Do you bring any news from the battlefield, {name}?

entries.name: Battle of Warsong Gulch
entries.how: The battle in Warsong Gulch rages on, {name}.  Do your part to drive the Silverwing Sentinels out of our lands!

entries.name: Field of Honor: Week 2
entries.how: You again, eh? Ready for the next test? I hope you aren't squeamish. You might need to bleed for this one... or preferably make the other guys bleed first.

entries.name: Field of Honor: Week 3
entries.how: I'm seein' some potential here. This next challenge will require you to really get your hands dirty. Hope you're up for it!

entries.name: Atal'ai Potent Potables
entries.how:
I offer quite a deal for you mon! Bring me mojo found only from de Atal'ai people, and I make you a proposition: power beyond your wildest imagination. Be warned, mon, this power can only be used de swamps it is found from. Dey say de Atal'ai practice forbidden hexcraft, and I might know a bit about 'em. 

Sound good? Do you want to make a trade?

entries.name: Jungle Durian
entries.how:
The bold and pungent smelling fruit will keep your spirits high while you traverse through the Swamp of Sorrows and explore the Temple of Atal'Hakkar. Don't let the odor fool you mon, this is a prized fruit of my people! 

If you bring me back something enticing from your adventures, I'll make it worth your while, mon. A bundle of our finest durian for your troubles! Shall we make a deal?

entries.name: Signets of the Lost Temple
entries.how:
For de most powerful adventurer, I offer de most powerful trades. I have somethin' that enhances your shoulder items, power from de Atal'ai themselves! {name}, if you have mojo found by the strongest of dere Atal'ai in da temple, I will make it worth your while. 

Let's not be too hasty now, I offer da fairest deals...

entries.name: Arathi Basin Resources!
entries.how:
War must be fought with soldiers, any soldier will tell you.  They'll also say that a battle fought with poor gear or on an empty stomach is lost before it starts!

That is why Arathi Basin is important.  There are key areas in the basin that hold essential resources.  Metals, weapons, food, lumber - all are needed, and all can be gained there.

That is what I want from you, {name}.  Enter Arathi Basin, win the battle by holding more bases than the enemy, and return to me with a crate of resources.

entries.name: More Resource Crates
entries.how: {name}, the League of Arathor has a standing mission for you to reenter Arathi Basin, procure more resource crates and bring them to me.

entries.name: The Battle for Arathi Basin!
entries.how:
{name}, the battle for Arathi Basin is a battle for resources and territory.  Key points in the area must be held and operated in order to supply our forces with much needed raw materials and supplies.  I charge you to assault the points farthest from our Arathi Basin base.

Assault the farm, the mine, the lumber mill and the blacksmith when they are controlled by the enemy.  Find the enemy's banner and rip it from its flag post!

When you have done this to all four points, return to me.

entries.name: Control Four Bases
entries.how:
{name}, you have taken the battle of Arathi Basin to our enemies and earned great honors in that field of battle.  You have shown us your worth as a {class}, and you have shown our enemies that we will not submit to their villainy!

Because of your proven value to us, I have a difficult task for you.  I want you to take and hold at least four of the bases in Arathi Basin.  If you can do that, then we will not only secure critical resources, we will show the Horde our dominance!

Go, {name}, and good fortune.

entries.name: Control Five Bases
entries.how:
{name}, battling for the resources of Arathi Basin is a bloody undertaking.  Your services to the League of Arathor are are needed as they are appreciated.

And we have one more task for you.

The League wishes to make one strong push against the Defilers' occupation of Arathi Basin.  We want them driven out of every strategic point on the battlefield!

It will not be easy, but if anyone can get it done, it is you.

entries.name: The Battle for Arathi Basin!
entries.how:
As you no doubt have heard, the League of Arathor is sending large numbers of troops into Arathi Basin.  Eager for food and supplies, these Alliance fools are intent to take and control the rich resources there.  We must show them that Arathi will never again be a home for humans!

Go to Arathi Basin and assault the mine, the lumber mill, the blacksmith and the stables.  Pull down the enemies' banners, declaring those territories for the Horde.

Go, {name}.  Report back to me when this task is complete.

entries.name: Take Four Bases
entries.how:
{name}, as the battles over Arathi Basin rage, news of your actions have reached many ears.  You are highly regarded among us, which gives me confidence that you will accomplish the mission I now have for you.

It is time to send a message to the League of Arathor.  We must show them that their holdings in Arathi Basin are tenuous and quickly lost.  We will show them this by holding, all at once, four strategic points in Arathi Basin.

Succeed in this, {name}, and earn great respect among the Defilers.

entries.name: Take Five Bases
entries.how:
It is difficult to see, so deep we are in the conflict, but our spies report a weakening in the League of Arathor's resolve.  We must use this window and strike a brutal blow against them!  Return to Arathi Basin and throw yourself against our foes.  Curse them and kill them and control all five strategic bases!  Send their soldiers screaming and bleeding from the front lines, with stories of your cruelty on their mewling lips.

Do this, and score a great victory for the Defilers.

entries.name: Cut Arathor Supply Lines
entries.how:
The League of Arathor is sparing no expense in their move to retake Arathi.  They, and all the races of the Alliance, now stream to this distant region, intent on expanding their hold from Refuge Pointe.  We must stop them, and the best means to stop them is to take their supplies.

You can help us, {name}.  Enter Arathi Basin, known for its rich mines, fertile land and skilled craftsman.  Capture and control every base you can, win the battle, and return to me with the resources you gain.

entries.name: More Resource Crates
entries.how: Although the Defilers have done well in breaking the supply lines of the League of Arathor, Alliance has proven quite stubborn in its want of Arathi Basin.  We must continue to send our own troops into the basin and come out with more of their resource crates.

entries.name: Conquering Arathi Basin
entries.how:
Our conflict with the Alliance has escalated to a true war.  No longer are false pretenses to enter into battle used or expected by either side at this point.

The battle for the Arathi Basin is one of resources, plain and simple.  Either the Alliance gets the resources and uses them against us or we get them and use them to keep our war efforts going.  Help the Defilers maintain the flow of resources we need, {name}!

entries.name: Claiming Arathi Basin
entries.how:
Winning a war is about more than just outsmarting and outfighting your opponent.  Victory often comes down to simply producing more than your enemy.

What we have in Arathi Basin is a sizeable supply of resources for whichever side manages to claim it first.

entries.name: Field of Honor: Week 4
entries.how:
How hard you can swing a blade or hurl a spell isn't the only measure of a fighter. Their ability to take in the battlefield and change tactics on the fly is just as important. 

You'll need that and more for this next challenge. Do you have that in you?

entries.name: Field of Honor: Week 5
entries.how: Different scenery, same wetwork. Let's test your, uh... consistency.

entries.name: Conqueror's Spaulders
entries.how:
It is said among us that the ornate shoulder armor worn by the mortal races started as an attempt to emulate the wings of a dragon.

Bring me the bindings worn by the highest Qiraji leaders and I shall shape them into a set of pauldrons more dreadful than even the wings of Nefarian himself!

entries.name: Signet of Unyielding Strength
entries.how:
The rings worn by the Qiraji lieutenants are rumored to grant them formidable abilities.  The corrupted gems that adorn them could, in theory, be swapped out with more pure materials to create uncorrupted versions of the rings.

The gems that adorn Qiraji idols would work quite well, as their quality is superior.

Bring me the ring and idols and I'll create a powerful ring for you, {class}.

entries.name: Drape of Unyielding Strength
entries.how:
I'm glad to hear you're aiding us in our attack on Ahn'Qiraj, {name}.  I can make you a protective item that'll be of assistance in the fight against our enemy, {class}.

I shall need a Qiraji drape, which I'll resize for you of course.  I'll also need idols and scarabs which I'll use to create a suitable clasp.

I promise you won't be disappointed.

entries.name: Sickle of Unyielding Strength
entries.how:
The Qiraji and their servants wield items made with the rarest and finest materials: bones from gargantuan ancient creatures, gems from the depths of the earth, metals pure and strong.

Just the sight of Qiraji artifacts fills me with an urge to practice my craft with their shattered and smelted pieces.  Prove your allegiance to the Circle, {name}, and I will make you a powerful weapon from the finest Qiraji materials.

entries.name: Conqueror's Greaves
entries.how:
Qiraji magic is strong and ancient.  The most powerful qiraji wield items of such might, they'd give pause even to a dragon.

Bring me the qiraji bindings of command and other minor components by and I'll create a set of powerful boots for you.

You will find them useful in the fight against the enemy.

entries.name: Conqueror's Legguards
entries.how:
You seek to prove your worth to my kind, mortal?  Very well, perhaps we can be of mutual assistance.

The ancient sandworm, Ouro, is a being of legendary power.  He is rumored to have been created by the Old God himself as a mockery of life.

His skin is unnatural... thick, nearly impregnable, yet it's flexible and allows him to move with the speed and grace of a much smaller creature.

Bring me a sample of his skin along with other minor components and I shall craft you leggings of great power.

entries.name: Conqueror's Crown
entries.how:
The Twin Emperors... their incessant whispers are slowly taking a toll on my sanity.  They mock me, knowing I cannot step further into their domain to save my brother Arygos.

In my visions I see their monstrous faces adorned by powerful crowns.  But I will have my revenge... I will transmute these symbols of Qiraji power to ones better suited to our needs.

Bring me the components I require, {name}.  I will give you a headpiece of unmatched power.

entries.name: Conqueror's Breastplate
entries.how:
The unmentionable Old God slowly awakens from his slumber beneath Ahn'Qiraj.  The terrible fate that awaits Azeroth could come in days or years; time has no meaning for beings of his power.

When the stars are favorable, he will lash out against all living beings with terrible wrath.  You must find him before then and find a way to bring his existence to an end.

Do this and bring me a piece of his husk.  I shall grant you armor no mortal has ever worn... armor fit for one who has slain a god!

entries.name: Mortal Champions
entries.how:
We sense the presence of our enslaved brethren deeper inside Ahn'Qiraj; yet not even an army of dragons would be enough to rescue them, {race}.

The same spell that imprisoned them would place us firmly under C'Thun's control should we come any closer to him.

The Old God has foreseen our arrival.  All hope is lost.  What difference could a mere mortal like you possibly make?

I shall need a Qiraji drape, which I'll resize for you of course.  I'll also need idols and scarabs which I'll use to create a suitable clasp.

I promise you won't be disappointed.

entries.name: Ring of Infinite Wisdom
entries.how:
The rings worn by the Qiraji lieutenants are rumored to grant them formidable abilities.  The corrupted gems that adorn them could, in theory, be swapped out with more pure materials to create uncorrupted versions of the rings.

The gems that adorn Qiraji idols would work quite well, as their quality is superior.

Bring me the ring and idols and I'll create a powerful ring for you, {class}.

entries.name: Gavel of Infinite Wisdom
entries.how:
The Qiraji and their servants wield items made with the rarest and finest materials: bones from gargantuan ancient creatures, gems from the depths of the earth, metals pure and strong.

Just the sight of Qiraji artifacts fills me with an urge to practice my craft with their shattered and smelted pieces.  Prove your allegiance to the Circle, {name}, and I will make you a powerful weapon from the finest Qiraji materials.

entries.name: Secrets of the Qiraji
entries.how: You have discovered an ancient Qiraji artifact! Perhaps one of the dragons near the entrance of the temple would have a use for this relic.

entries.name: Imperial Qiraji Armaments
entries.how:
We have not sat idly by for a millennium, {name}.

We have watched these beasts feast on their own when they have exhausted their utility. We have listened as they have plotted and schemed to destroy our world. And we have learned of their own internal treachery.

Weaknesses exist and we know how to use those weaknesses to our advantage.

Find and bring me their ceremonial armaments: Combined with the element created from the volatility of their own God, they will become a force of reckoning.

entries.name: Imperial Qiraji Regalia
entries.how:
Arygos theorizes that the element which is born of conflicts between the Old Gods and their minions is also extremely deadly to them under the right conditions. I speak of Elementium, mortal.

Find and bring me Imperial Qiraji Regalia and the toxic element and I shall infuse weapons of great power.

entries.name: C'Thun's Legacy
entries.how:
The walls of Ahn'Qiraj tremble. A force of evil, older than the world itself, has been destroyed.

As you look at the remnants of the colossal abomination your heart nearly freezes. Even in death you can feel the legacy of C'Thun's evil around you.

You have done what was thought to be impossible.

You grab at an eye stalk of the fiend, stowing it safely in your pack.

Take the Eye of C'Thun to the dragons in the next chamber.

entries.name: The Savior of Kalimdor
entries.how: To the Caverns of Time you go, Lord {name}. Anachronos awaits your return. Give him the eye of C'Thun as he will undoubtedly wish to place it in his master's collection.

entries.name: Desert Power
entries.how: The deep and dark tunnels to ancient places of the world are ill suited for your travel.

entries.name: Time-Mender Aedormi
entries.how: You've proven yourself to be a dependable ally in recent days, {name}. To that end, another agent of the Bronze Dragonflight may be in need of your aid. This dragon is known as Time-Mender Aedormi and you'll find her near the gates to Anh'Qiraj, patrolling in the skies. Use this flare to call her down and learn of her mission.

entries.name: The Fugitive
entries.how:
I've come to this timeline in search of a dangerous agent of the void. This creature has wreaked havoc across their own timeline and I fear that they will do the same here. I've followed a trail of voidstuff to this place but the trail has gone cold, which is why I'd like to enlist your aid.

Nearby, there is a camp of Twilight's Hammer cultists. This creature has a way of influencing susceptible minds, so keep an eye out for anything that would be out of place, even for deranged cultist types.

entries.name: The Fall of Ossirian
entries.how:
A terrible menace has been laid to rest. The cruel Ossirian has been vanquished.

The denizens of Kalimdor would be relieved to know of this victory. Take Ossirian's head and present it to Commander Mar'alith of Cenarion Hold.

entries.name: Echoes of War
entries.how:
Five years since the last war...

Tens of thousands of lives were lost and for what? The threat was never fully extinguished.

And so the Lich King stirs once more... His yes-man, Kel'Thuzad, amassing for another attack upon our lands.

We will not allow it! Prove your dedication. Prove that you are willing to risk life and limb to stop this madness and the combined might of the Dawn and the Crusade will be at your beck and call.

Enter Naxxramas and destroy the Scourge within...

entries.name: Cryptstalker Tunic
entries.how:
I have discovered a use for the carapace of the crypt fiend. I am able to fashion an extremely light and very deadly set of armor by combining the fragments with some of the desecrated magical armors lost in Naxxramas.

Bring me the items I require and I shall fashion for you a suit of armor the likes of which has never before been seen in our world!

entries.name: Earthshatter Tunic
entries.how:
Would you honor me by returning the armor of those that fell in the defense of these lands?

The armor has been desecrated and is undoubtedly being used for evil; however, with wartorn armor scraps, the desecrated armor can be renewed and worn for battle once more.

Bring me the remnants of the fallen along with purification materials and Earthshatter shall be yours to don.

Search Naxxramas.

entries.name: Bonescythe Breastplate
entries.how:
If you want Bonescythe made, you're going to have to supply the materials.

Enter Naxxramas, the big floating city of death in the sky up there, and find desecrated armor and wartorn armor scraps. Bring those back along with the materials to put everything together and you'll have your Bonescythe. Oh, and you'll need to pay me for my troubles... I'll supply the bones.

entries.name: Dreamwalker Tunic
entries.how:
Many heroes fell in the last war and many continue to perish at the hands of the Scourge to this day. From the corpses of the fallen, the armor is stripped and taken back to Naxxramas to be used for unknown purposes.

Recover the desecrated armor and wartorn armor scraps and supply to me the other material components I require and I will craft Dreamwalker armor.

entries.name: Frostfire Robe
entries.how:
As a Watcher, I was allowed access to many of Medivh's personal effects. Among those items, I found the tomes most enlightening. While the majority of the books were filled with - to put it bluntly - tripe, there were some gems. One of those tomes documented the creation of a set of armor fit for an archmage: Frostfire.

<Angela points to her head.>

It's all in here and I am willing to share the fruits of that knowledge with you as long as you are able to provide me with the necessary materials.

entries.name: Plagueheart Robe
entries.how:
I make no pretenses, maggot. The darkness Plagueheart items hold could very well destroy the both of us. That is why the price is so high. If I'm going to die, it's going to be as a rich man.

And I don't give an ounce of gnoll spit how you die, only that you do as I ask. Bring me what I require and we will both benefit - or die; but I've already explained this...

entries.name: Robe of Faith
entries.how:
<Father Montoy makes some strange gestures in the air in front of you.>

Blessed boy, have you found the vestments of the fallen? The poor souls whose last breaths were taken on the field of battle - stripped of everything including their dignity.

Bring me the desecrated remnants of the departed along with reagents of purification and you shall know faith.

entries.name: The Fall of Kel'Thuzad
entries.how:
The phylactery is all that remains of the master of Naxxramas. Your better judgment dictates that you destroy the phylactery, preventing the lich from ever reforming. Thankfully, you seldom listen to that internal voice of reason.

Someone at Light's Hope will pay you hugely for this artifact. Who cares if Kel'Thuzad regenerates to full power?

entries.name: The Fate of Ramaladni
entries.how:
Ramaladni was a warrior of the Brotherhood - a pupil of Highlord Mograine before the Dawn even existed! When news of Mograine's death reached him, hatred and anger took over.

Understand this, {name}, when rage and retribution take the reins, a man ceases to be a man. The man personifies the emotions that control him instead. And so it would be that Ramaladni, the spirit of retribution, would enter Naxxramas to exact vengeance... and never return.

Enter Naxxramas and find what became of Ramaladni.

entries.name: Ramaladni's Icy Grasp
entries.how: Fixing this band may prove to be quite challenging, {name}. You see, it was made from the very runes that form inside Scourge structures - like Naxxramas. Additional materials are also required but your main concern should be getting those frozen runes. Bring me what I need and I will restore the ring to its former glory.

entries.name: The Only Song I Know...
entries.how:
You fancy yourself a hero of the Dawn, eh? I've seen our greatest soldiers get rolled over by Kel'Thuzad's plebes! How well could someone so clueless possibly fare in Naxxramas?

<Wilhelm sighs.>

Bah, what choice do I got? You're the best I can do; I may as well help you.

Omarion left me with one recipe. It's the only song I know... I can make a few variations of these pants; you just gotta supply the materials.

entries.name: Omarion's Handbook
entries.how:
Wilhelm,

If you are reading this, I have perished - finally. I want you to know that my dying thoughts revolved around you and your ineptitude when it comes to tradeskills. Unfortunately, the bearer of this handbook is in even worse shape than you in regards to crafting.

About the book: These are the rest of my recipes. Make the bearer of this book whatever they request. I'm sure you will charge a hefty fee for your services because you are, after all, a bastard.

In Disdain,

Omarion

entries.name: Icebane Gauntlets
entries.how: Thanks to you and Omarion, may he rest in peace, I am now able to create Icebane gauntlets. All you need to do is bring me the materials and pay a small crafting fee.

entries.name: The Power in Death
entries.how:
{name}, I have a task for you.

Within this citadel lies a dark art that breeds despair in mortal hearts and pushes everything towards a state of death and decay. Kel'Thuzad and his underlings possess a singular affinity for this power.. the essence of death itself.

Bring me a sample of this energy, so that I may study it. In my current state, I care not for what it does to me...

entries.name: The Power in Death
entries.how:
Death holds sway over every living thing.. it isn't something you can run from when it comes for you.

Yet even in this evil, I believe we can extract power from its essence through the form of deathstones.

Investigate Naxxramas further and gather me more information.

entries.name: Book of Deathstones
entries.how: You open the aged and weathered tome and discover text detailing a necromantic ritual. Perhaps Archmage Tarsis would be interested in having this information.

entries.name: Curious Karazhan Curios!
entries.how: Now that you've figured out a way into the crypt, I'd like to ask you a favor. In case it wasn't obvious I'm an archaeologist in employ of the Royal Library of Stormwind. I collect artifacts and relics from all across the world for academic research and study, and I'm keenly interested in any such curios you may come across within the depths of the crypt. Bring any that you think might be interesting back to me, and I'll make it worth your while.

entries.how: Now that you've figured out a way into the crypt, I'd like to ask you a favor. In case it wasn't obvious I'm an archaeologist in employ of the Royal Library of Stormwind. I collect artifacts and relics from all across the world for academic research and study, and I'm keenly interested in any such curios you may come across within the depths of the crypt. Bring any that you think might be interesting back to me, and I'll make it worth your while.

entries.name: For Gold and Glory!
entries.how:
Calling all adventurers and treasure hunters! Let it be known that the Kirin Tor has authorized the disbursement of considerable funds to any individuals who are able to descend into the crypts below Karazhan and recover a particular  magical artifact. Any other treasure, curios, or coin recovered is of no consequence to the order, and may be retained as additional compensation.  Interested parties should report to... 

<The bottom of the note has been torn off and the rest of the details are missing.>

entries.name: No Ordinary Shadows
entries.how:
A sudden and oppressive darkness begins to fall over you as you kneel down. You notice that all nearby light seems to darken and fade as the darkness seems to reach out to you. These are no natural shadows. 

A quick glance over to the entrance to the crypt nearby tells you without doubt that this malign darkness is coming from the crypt itself, with inky black tendrils seeking more light to snuff out. You shudder as hairs on the back of your neck stand up.

entries.name: Seeking Survivors
entries.how:
Oh, I see. Yes, the body you claim to have found does indeed seem to match my recollection of one of the adventurers who passed through here recently. There were five of them, as I recall. I urged them against going any further, but they could not be dissuaded. It seems my warnings were well-founded as I've not seen any of their number pass by since. I feared the worst and, well...

You say she was the only body you found? If that's true, mayhap there are other survivors somewhere in the pass?

entries.name: To the Rescue
entries.how:
<The man's one open eye locks with yours.>

Psst, hey you. Yes, you! Think you can get me out of here? I've been lying here playing dead for hours but its only a matter of time before these damned ogres remember I'm here and come to eat me, or worse! 

This cage is locked up pretty tight but one of these brutes should have the key. See if you can find one and let me out. I'd certainly be in your debt. 

I'm going to keep playing dead while you get to work. Now go... quietly!

entries.name: Are You Afraid of the Dark?
entries.how:
Really can't thank you enough for the help back there. You really saved my bacon. 

I've been chatting with this nice young woman while waiting for you and I think she might have some ideas to help you get into that forsaken crypt, if you really do insist on pushing your luck.

I'm getting ahead of myself. though. I believe I owe you some information.

entries.name: The Hypothesis
entries.how: I think I can fashion a magical totem of sorts that should allow you to pierce this malign darkness and at least allow you to explore the crypts. I don't have all of the components with me, however. Some of this might not be easy to find, but judging by what I've seen from you so far, I trust that you are resourceful enough to secure what is needed.

entries.name: Testing Our Hypothesis
entries.how:
I think it wise that we put this device to the test before you commit fully to your delve down into the darkness of the Crypts. Take the torch to the edge of the magical darkness and activate it. See if it serves its purpose and provides illumination, and more importantly, discern how it behaves when exposed to this magic.

This totem was bound with a specific purpose and should be compelled to adhere to that purpose, but there's no real telling until we get there and test this hypothesis.

entries.name: The Violet Satchel
entries.how: You've found a small violet satchel that appears to bear the mark of the Kirin Tor. Despite your best efforts, you can't seem to find a way to lift the flap and see what is inside, however. The note on the body of the adventurer where you found this suggests that it might be the property of Archmage Kir-Moldir of Dalaran. It might be worth your while to seek out the Archmage and return his property... and claim the promised reward.

entries.name: A Void Path
entries.how:
Show my Eye of Kilrogg the way out of this ravine and back to the Ashenvale road. Keep it moving and I'll follow once I see a clear path.

I'll stay here--one of us should keep our bearings. If you lose the way, I can guide you back through the eye. I will not have us both wandering blind in this malicious forest.

I can hold the channel for four minutes. No longer. Reach the road before the vision breaks, or return to me and we try again.

entries.name: Unrest at Tyr's Hand
entries.how:
There's been an interesting development, {name}. It seems that while the Scarlet Crusade's focus was aimed at Naxxramas, there's been some sort of unrest in the ranks at Tyr's Hand. Details are spotty for now, but from what we understand, there has been some infighting amongst the crusaders.

I'd like to send you to the camp west of Tyr's Hand to assess the situation out for us. Let us know what you find as soon as possible.

entries.name: The Schism
entries.how:
I'll cut straight to the chase; the Tyr's Hand enclave is no longer under our control. While we were away at Naxxramas, a force of  hostile crusaders came in from the city of Stratholme and took control of the stronghold. We've been barred entry and any emissaries we send in do not return.

I am loathe to ask for external assistance, but something is very wrong and I don't know if we can reclaim the enclave alone.

entries.name: The Scarlet Reclamation
entries.how:
<Leonid's expression darkens when you confirm that Caldoran is present at the Scarlet Base Camp. After a moment, he regains his composure.> 

Thank... thank you, {name}. For now, continue to assist Beatrix if you are willing. I will confer with Lord Tyrosus and develop contingencies should the Argent Dawn need to become directly involved. I pray that the situation is not as dire as we've been led to believe but if we need to step in and put an end to this, we will be ready.

entries.name: Gathering Intelligence
entries.how:
I am not pleased to engage you for aid. You consort with the heretic and the unclean and it is beneath me and our sacred order to entertain your presence here. However... you seem adequately capable and will prove to be a useful instrument here for our needs.

Go to Tyr's Hand and scout the cathedral there before moving deeper into New Avalon to scout the rear keep and mage tower. Return here without delay and report what you find. We need to know what we are up against.

entries.name: Weakening The Defenses
entries.how:
While you were away we finalized our attack plans on Tyr's Hand. We will execute a frontal assault as well as a flanking strike, which I myself will lead. Before we fully commit we'll need to weaken the forward defenses. I'm sending you back in to Tyr's Hand to take out as many of the enemy Siege Commanders as possible, as they are the key organizers of the enclave's defenses. 

I'm leaving to join my forces at our position now. You'll report to Commander Beatrix when you return. 

Don't fail.

entries.name: Report to Lord Tyrosus
entries.how: Please, {name}, a messenger just arrived. You must return to Light's Hope Chapel with all haste! We are under attack and Lord Maxwell Tyrosus has requested your presence at once.

entries.name: The Wrath of the Dawn
entries.how:
Regardless of the reason that beast withdrew back to the enclave, we will not give it another chance to destroy us. It seems that our hand is forced and we must now commit the full fury of the Argent Dawn to the cause of ending the threat of the Scarlet Enclave.  

Go back to the Scarlet Base Camp and meet back up with Beatrix. Let her know that she has our support... for now.

entries.name: Decapitation Strike
entries.how:
Our forces are mustered and we will move into positions to begin the forward attack while your forces sneak around to the rear of the cathedral using the mountain path.

Once inside make your way to the abbey and ring the bell to signal the attack. 

You'll be in the thickest of the fighting until we arrive to relieve you, so take care.

entries.name: Red = Dead
entries.how:
It seems that the beast that attacked light's hope is Caldoran's pet and the attack on Light's Hope was merely a ruse to draw our forces out and commit us to this attack. Caldoran and Beatrix sought to use us to create a distraction and remove a rival in Balnazzar, and then turn on us and remove us as a presence in the Plaguelands after they regained control. 

We don't have all of the answers and it's looking grim, but we will put these dogs down for this treachery.

entries.name: Fall of the Grand Crusader
entries.how:
The path forward now is simple and brutal. Breach the inner sanctum of the Scarlet Enclave and confront the new self-proclaimed "Grand Crusader"  Baelin Caldoran. Bring him to justice for his crimes. We'll stay here and secure this position to ensure that no remnant forces harass you from behind. 

Bring that monster to justice.

entries.name: The Corrupted Emblem
entries.how:
<Sifting through the ruins of the battle with Baelin Caldoran, you find the emblem from the shattered blade of the Ashbringer. As you hold the skull-shaped icon in your hand, you can swear you hear a slight,  murmuring whisper. You look around, searching for a source for the voice, but you see no obvious source of the sound. You shake your head and stow the emblem in your pack.>

Seek out Lord Maxwell Tyrosus once you make your return to Light's Hope Chapel. He will be interested in this artifact.

entries.name: Sinew of Light
entries.how:
Grok'lo will arrange a meeting with special crafter once you find a suitable string to go with that giant bat wing.

Grok'lo recommend finding best string possible.

<Grok'lo smiles under his helmet>

Dragon Sinew definitely best string.

entries.name: Food Shortage
entries.how:
<The chef begins speaking before you could manage a simple greeting.>

Thank the light, help finally arrived! Neither the stove nor the pantry can keep up with the sudden surge in orders coming in. Something happened that cut off our usual supply lines, and I assume all the screaming outside has something to do with it.

Whatever the reason, I need assistance. Now. Fetch me whatever looks vaguely edible from around town and we'll go from there.

entries.name: Wrangling Apples
entries.how:
If you ask me, fresh fruit is the highlight of any meal. Apples are my favorite, and conveniently we have a thriving orchard south of here.

Assuming it hasn't caught fire yet - which is a distinct possibility - I'll bet it's about time for a harvest!

Normally the farmhands are willing to cut me a discount, but I still owe them a pie. Getting them for cheap is out of the question, but you look like you can afford them.

entries.name: Fish in a Barrel
entries.how:
I served in Hearthglen for a time, and I cannot tell you how utterly terrifying it was relying on deliveries from across the Plaguelands to keep us fed. New Avalon having a stable supply chain by sea has been a blessing, at least until very recently.

In yet another case of "Carrie is trying to feed an army with a kitchen stocked for a family", I am in need of fish. Check the dock down south to see if my order has arrived.

entries.name: Main Course
entries.how:
No meal is truly complete without the star of the dish - the meat! As you can probably imagine, hunting for meat that is safe to consume in the Plaguelands is a challenge unlike no other.

To make matters worse, our hounds eat nothing but meat! I am sure you can see where this is going, and I am sure by now you understand why I am perpetually behind.

Well? What are you waiting for?

entries.name: Prove Your Worth: Headgear
entries.how:
Staying on top of your trade is crucial for maintaining a high standard of quality. Our soldiers entrust their lives to unnamed craftsmen, and to me for ensuring the quality of every piece of armor.

My task for you is simple. If you are well practiced in Tailoring, Leatherworking, or Blacksmithing, then craft a piece of headgear, purely for your own benefit. You are free to keep the result.

If you lack the skill, commission and donate any piece of the crusade's uniform instead.

entries.name: Preposterously Prosed Postage
entries.how:
To the Esteemed Head Chef of New Avalon: Carrie Hearthfire,

I trust this letter finds you in good spirits! Your departure from Hearthglen has left a hole in our hearts, and in our stomachs. Not a day passes by without a complaint of the morning gruel, yearning for the next delightful meal.

To that end we are planning a banquet; one which we intend to serve only the finest dishes in Lordaeron: yours.

An escorted caravan will arrive in a fortnight. You and your meals ought best be prepared.

entries.name: The Great Feast
entries.how:
Your assistance has been invaluable. The citizens and soldiers of New Avalon can count on a hot meal tonight, and for many nights that follow. You have my gratitude, truly.

However, as you apparently read yourself, I have one last task to tend to before I can finally put my feet up. I can handle most of this myself, but if you're willing to do me one more favor, I will teach you my most famous recipes.

You will be eating like a Highlord every night.

entries.name: VIP Haute Club Membership
entries.how:
Hey, you!

You look like the person Carrie had been speaking of recently. She said many good things about you. Well, not at first, but she quickly changed her tone.

Anyway, friends of the chef are friends of mine. I'd like to grant you a permanent membership, and you won't need to carry that card around all the time.

All I ask in return is a Sunrise Omelette and a Prowler Steak. Both cooked by your hand, of course.

entries.name: Pin Cushion
entries.how:
Whoa! Awfully brave to be stomping around the shooting grounds amidst our training. You're practically begging for a projectile to the knee, or maybe your behind given the way you're shuffling around.

But hey, your safety is your prerogative. Since you seem like a real risk taker, why not lend us a helping hand? Gathering our arrows after every round of shots takes away from precious shooting time.

How about you go grab a few for me, eh?

entries.name: Bullet Heaven
entries.how:
You might be thinking, "but what if I wanted an ammo pouch instead," and "if I say something, will she make me stand in front of bullets too?" I can't read your mind, but a good ranger is great at making predictions.

Truth is: we don't use bullets around here, despite my advocacy of such. Were a pile of bullets to, say, land at my feet, I suppose I would have no choice but to design a proper pouch to contain them.

If only.

entries.name: Holy Threads
entries.how:
This loom is special. Did you know that? All of our craftsmen had their tools of the trade blessed by our high priests.

In particular, the loom attracts stray fabrics and thread destined to be used in the holiest of our ceremonial vestments. Over time, we will have enough gathered to create a new robe, and these days are a cause for celebration, for me at least.

If you are interested in the process for your own curiosity, thread some bolts near the loom and watch the Light at work.

entries.name: Red is Not Dead
entries.how:
Hm, speaking of secrets, I have been working on a new project: luxury packs for our highest ranking soldiers. They must be large, crafted from the finest silks, and most importantly, as red as the crest of the Scarlet Crusade.

The material is the easy part, I intend to use your dawnwoven threads for this. Finding the perfect dye, however, is well beyond my capabilities. Scour the world in search of the perfect red hue and I'll consider you a partner in this endeavor by sharing my final design with you.

entries.name: New Avalon
entries.how:
As you've seen, New Avalon boasts a significant military presence but it also offers safety and security to civilians.

If you can cobble together a more permanent disguise, consider offering a helping hand. Ingratiating yourself with the folk there could be beneficial to our efforts to reclaim the enclave, to say nothing of putting you in a position to "appropriate" some of the material and resources there, enriching yourself and depriving their war machine of crucial supplies.

entries.name: An Apple a Day Keeps the Undead at Bay
entries.how:
It is good to see you again. I have had no troubles keeping the kitchen stocked since you have been away, but I did notice this morning that I am just shy enough apples to make a pie. I thought it was time to give myself a little treat.

If you can spare a few minutes, could you stop by the orchard and grab a few? Unfortunately I still haven't made Johnny's pie yet either, but I can't make a pie without apples and I won't waste apples on Johnny's pie!

I will, of course, share a slice with you.

entries.name: Fish On Demand
entries.how:
I hate fish. I cannot stand the smell of them. They are extremely creepy. Truly the worst.

Since this is my kitchen, I can and do exercise my authority to say NO to fish imports, but sometimes our soldiers get it in their heads that they need a fisherman's feast.

Tonight is one of those nights it would seem. I need fish, on the double!

entries.name: Food Safety
entries.how:
I seem to recall one of the ingredients that I sent you to collect when we first met was the meat. I also seem to recall a lot of complaints that night about their meals making them sick? It was the strangest thing.

Anyway, the larder is running low on meats again and it would be nice to know that I have someone trustworthy to help replenish it. The last thing I need is to be expecting a delivery only to find out a week after the fact that the courier died!

entries.name: Familiar Foulness
entries.how:
<You have found a vial of foul, viscous liquid on a laboratory table. It was surrounded by various ingredients that have been meticulously measured and diced into careful portions. Though the herbs are unidentifiable, one undamaged and discolored beast heart rests nearby.

The concoction is familiar, reminiscent of recent experiments performed by the Royal Apothecary Society. If your curiosity overpowers your disgust, perhaps one of their members may be interested in your discovery.>

entries.name: Oh, My Bleeding Hearts!
entries.how:
I assume you are well acclimated to the Plaguelands given the impressive taint present on your specimens. It only stands to reason that you understand how inconvenient it is for any lone member of the Royal Apothecary Society to cross the Bulwark for supplies.

Renferrel claims to have an interest in bleeding hearts, the flower, in addition to once-beating hearts. I am unsure whether it is for alchemical research or their visual appeal, but I know he would appreciate a delivery of various hearts.

entries.name: Unfamiliar Foulness
entries.how:
<You have found a vial of foul, viscous liquid on a laboratory table. It was surrounded by various ingredients that have been meticulously measured and diced into careful portions. Though the herbs are unidentifiable, one undamaged and discolored beast heart rested nearby.

Alchemists in Darnassus might have an idea of how to tap into whatever restorative properties might be present in the potion. You should also bring them some flowers, as to not come barreling into a shop with just a pile of hearts.>

entries.name: A Green Sample
entries.how:
If you're going to bother me you can at least make yourself useful. I have an errand I need run.

For a city of mages, Dalaran has a surprising interest in botany. The Kirin Tor keep to themselves, but I would love a sample of their mana-infused vegetation.

You're clearly someone who is comfortable being where people don't want you, maybe you could find a way into the city. If you do, bring me back whatever is growing in their central garden.

entries.name: Starving Arcane
entries.how:
The breach has affected many of our factotums and enchantments throughout the city, including many that are seeing to our defenses. This fragmented arcane energy has spoken to rogue elementals who seek to saturate themselves in this free flowing magic.

While we are busy tending to the wards and other major incidents, it would be a favor to the Kirin Tor if you could cull this elemental throng.

entries.name: Heart of Disruption
entries.how:
Whatever disturbed the leylines, it started at the top of the Violet Citadel. A thunderous crash rang out from the parlors above, and now we are overrun with rampant arcane power. It's taking all we have just to keep the wards in place.

We cannot afford to stall any longer. We need help.

The Kirin Tor are busy inside, but you will still need a less public approach to gain entry. Take this key and meet me in the citadel once you've made your way into the city. We must put an end to this disruption.

entries.name: Power Overwhelming
entries.how:
The Kirin Tor have long been allies of the Alliance. With the destruction of their city at the hands of the arch demon Archimonde, the once proud city of mages has now become reclusive and distrusting of outsiders.

In recent years they have begun reconstruction efforts to bring the city of Dalaran back to its former glory. However, reports show they are struggling to contain an outbreak of wayward arcane energies.

We must help them disperse these attacks lest we lose one of our most powerful allies.

entries.name: Heart of Disruption
entries.how:
You may not have our best interests at heart, but I won't deny an extra pair of hands. And if Dalaran falls, it takes everything with it--including your Undercity.

So, your benefactor wants in? Fine. I'll imbue your key to work past my wards so you can enter the city. Once you're in, meet me at the Violet Citadel where this all began. With everything going on the Kirin Tor will be too busy to stop you.

Scavenge what you will, but whatever happens, our first priority is to prevent a catastrophe.

entries.name: The Grave Knight
entries.how:
Within the underbelly of the mage city to the north is a traitor to our kind. A necromancer of disturbing talent. He raises an army of undeath right under the Kirin Tor's nose.

I care not for the fate of the mage city, {name}, but this grave knight spits in the face of everything we Forsaken stand for. Put an end to him. Show him no one is beyond the reach of the Dark Lady.

entries.name: Opportunistic Education
entries.how:
Well if it ain't a like-minded entrepreneur. Sneakin' into Dalaran durin' such troublesome times? Tsk tsk.

My kinda {race}!

While our mage friends here are occupied, maybe we could find ourselves some 'misplaced' treasures. They gots whole libraries dedicated to fancy arcane magics. If you could bring me one of their secret tomes, I could sell it for a pretty penny. Split the profits with ya.

Hey hey don't look at me like that. You ain't exactly here on a field trip yourself. You want in or what?

entries.name: Source of Power
entries.how:
With the city of Dalaran under siege by their own constructs, this is the perfect opportunity to, let's say, borrow a few samples.

Imagine an army of arcane-powered abominations. The Dark Lady would have no choice but to recognize my alchemical prowess. Maybe even grant me head of the Royal Apothecary Society?

Go to the city and find the constructs' cores. They are unlikely to give them willingly, so do what you must.

entries.name: The Drowned City
entries.how:
What I am about to ask you is no small feat, {class}, and will likely require strong allies to accomplish.

I want to know more about the ruins on the other side of the cavern the naga are guarding. If my suspicions prove correct, it could indeed be the lost city of I'lalai. The amount of lost historical knowledge at our fingertips could be unrivaled, but I am too old to venture myself.

Enter the ruins and gather etchings of any tablets you find there, then return to me.

entries.name: The Only Good Brinescale...
entries.how:
You have done well to slay the naga just off of our coast, but the fact that they are in our waters in such numbers means there is yet a larger threat.

I have spoken to Kin'weelay, and he thinks these Brinescale naga are infiltrating the ruins of the Drowned City. If the naga are there, then they are up to no good and are likely searching for something.

We can't let them get their hands on anything that could compromise us here and it is time to put an end to this. Slay their leader and return to me.

entries.name: Take Two With Water
entries.how:
<Loremaster Dibbs' hands shake as he reads the scouting report and the troll legends.>

Could it be? By this account it sounds like the lost troll city of I'lalai has risen just off the coast of Stranglethorn! We must investigate immediately. Why, if my research is correct this could be the archeological discovery of the century!

Please, I know it is a long trek back to Stranglethorn but if you find yourself in this Drowned City, collect any legends you find there and return them to me.

entries.name: Magics of the Drowned City
entries.how:
The Skullsplitter fetishes Brother Nimetz sent with you are indeed powerful, though I do not think they contributed to Kurzen's condition, or at least not directly.

Still, if the rumors are true and the lost troll city of I'lalai has indeed risen from its watery grave, it is possible the dark magics used to raise the doomed city may be related.

If you dare to venture into the Drowned City of I'lalai, please gather any troll fetishes you find and bring them here to me for further study.

entries.name: Shady Saltseers
entries.how:
Hey pal, you look like you can handle yourself in a fight.

Baron Revilgaz has me keep'n my ear to the ground for magical objects. Word on the street is that a sunken troll ruin has mysteriously become, eh, un-sunk, which means there are a lot of unclaimed goods, if you catch my meaning.

Problem is, it's also caught the eye of pirates! Not just any pirates, the Saltseers specifically collect magical artifacts. I need you to go into the Drowned City, clear them out and take their stolen artifacts.

entries.name: The Saltseer Captain
entries.how:
The Saltseer pirates have been a thorn in my side recently and knowing they're in the Drowned City makes it worse! I mean they're always bad news, but there is one captain in particular I want outta the picture. That damned Captain Dreadrise!

He and his crew are very accomplished at gathering all the magical artifacts I've been after, and I'm tired of the competition.

I want you to remove Captain Dreadrise and his Saltseer Coroners from the picture. Permanently.

entries.name: Ancient Gurubashi Idol
entries.how:
The ancient Gurubashi of Stranglethorn Vale were da masters of dark blood magics. Rumors be they'd use pure truesilver idols to channel that bad bad voodoo.

Ol' Mazu'kon would love to get his hands on one of those idols... for academics ya see. How 'bout you gather some friends and do a bit of smash and grab on that drowned city stickin' out the ocean off the coast of Stranglethorn? Kill the most impressive lookin' priest ya can find in there, and they sure to have what I be lookin' for.

entries.name: Ancient Gurubashi Secrets
entries.how:
Lan'dalock and I have been discussing a recent development in the south seas involving an ancient Gurubashi ruin that has suddenly appeared off the coast of Stranglethorn Vale.

Such a site has significant archeological value. We'd be highly interested in obtaining one of the idols that certain witch doctors amongst the ancient Gurubashi would use as a ritual focus for their blood magic.

Enter this "Drowned City" and recover one of these idols for us.

entries.name: Blackmaw Reclamation
entries.how:
Will you aid us in our final battle, {race}, and be a savior to the Blackmaw?

Varrox Bleakhoof, bane of the Blackmaw: a demon whose appetite for destruction will never be satisfied. His corruption consumes all that it touches. Even now, he and his underlings continue to lay waste to our burrows.

We've come far in our fight against the Legashi, but for the Blackmaw to ever have a future, Varrox must fall.

Find him in Blackmaw Hold, and strike him down. Only then can the Blackmaw finally be at peace.

entries.name: The Twin Bears
entries.how:
When the Legashi invaded, many precious things were left behind in the commotion. Of particular value to me are two totems. They depict legends of our twin gods, Ursoc and Ursol.

I know our immediate survival is of greatest concern, but we must also think of saving our people's history.

Those totems are likely still in our former hold. If they are, you would be doing a great kindness by returning them to me.

entries.name: Feeding Time!
entries.how:
You have certainly proven yourself to me, {name}, but the others of my tribe are less easily persuaded. For that, you will need to continue your efforts against the Legashi.

Bring to me the horns of slain Legashi satyr. Every bundle you bring me will serve as a symbol of your service to the Blackmaw.

entries.name: Claws That Rend, Tusks that Gore
entries.how:
Two behemoths patrol the place the Blackmaw once called home: Bonesnout, the Unbroken and Withermaw, the great bear. Generations of hunters have tried to fell them, and all have failed.

I take no joy in asking you to slay these magnificent beasts, but my people need to be able to return home. The least I can do is ensure their deaths are not in vain. If you bring me their remains, I will fashion a weapon in memory of their strength.

entries.name: A Lost Memento
entries.how:
The necklace is adorned with miscellaneous charms: scraps of feathers, acorn shells, and colorful pebbles. Its leather strap is torn. The ornamentation suggests it belonged to a Furbolg, while its small size and rough quality indicate a child's handiwork.

There's a chance the necklace is of some sentimental value to one of the Blackmaw. It may be good to find the owner and return it.

entries.name: Get to the Roots of It
entries.how:
The burrow you speak of is a tunnel to Blackmaw Hold. In the past, the furbolg have guarded it fiercely, making it inaccessible to outsiders. With this satyr situation, however, we can get inside.

So close to Nordrassil, there would be actively growing roots. Older roots can be seen on the world's surface, but newer ones can only be found deep underground. Little is known of their magical properties.

If you were to bring me some samples to study, the druids of Thunder Bluff would be in your debt.

entries.name: Get to the Roots of It
entries.how:
The burrow you speak of is a tunnel to Blackmaw Hold. In the past, the furbolg have guarded it fiercely, making it inaccessible to outsiders. With this satyr situation, however, we can get inside.

So close to Nordrassil, there would be actively growing roots. Older roots can be seen on the world's surface, but newer ones can only be found deep underground. Little is known of their magical properties.

If you were to bring me some samples to study, the Cenarion Circle would be in your debt.

entries.name: Blackmaw Pouches
entries.how: Every bundle you recover will serve as a symbol of your service to my people.

entries.name: Blackmaw Magic
entries.how:
The Blackmaw furbolgs in the mountains overlooking Azshara have been dabbling in dark magic. While a primitive people being corrupted by demonic magic is nothing new for Azeroth, Lan'dalock and I would like to study their spell foci.

Travel to the stronghold known as Blackmaw Hold and recover one of the Blackmaw Ritual Totems for us. Only the most powerful of the Blackmaw's shamans will be carrying one of these, so bring allies and take care.

entries.name: Blackmaw Magic
entries.how:
The Blackmaw furbolgs in the mountains overlooking Azshara have been corrupted by dark and sinister magic. We do not know the full extent of the corruption and what impact it may have upon the elements in the area, but we hope to understand it better.

Travel to the stronghold known as Blackmaw Hold and recover one of the Blackmaw Ritual Totems for us. Only the most powerful of the Blackmaw's shamans will be carrying one of these, so bring allies and prepare for a difficult battle.

entries.name: Blackmaw Pouches
entries.how:
It breaks my heart to admit, but my brothers and sisters inside Blackmaw Hold are irreparably corrupted.

If you bring me some of their personal belongings, I can at least give their families something to remember them by. Every bundle you recover will serve as a symbol of your service to my people.

entries.name: More Unstable Magic
entries.how: Bring me any additional motes of unstable magic you encounter in your travels. Any data we can glean from such fragments will be invaluable to the Kirin Tor.

entries.name: Unstable Magic
entries.how:
Archmage Rhonin is presently abroad investigating a disturbance in the flow of magic across Azeroth. The Archmage has charged me with soliciting the aid of strong adventurers like yourself in gathering important field data to aid him.

Take this Arcane Censer. While afflicted by its magic, you will be able to extract motes of unstable magic from the most skilled spell casters and other singularly powerful entities you may encounter. Bring me said motes and the Kirin Tor will be in your debt.

entries.name: A Taste of Home
entries.how:
Are you familiar with Silvermoon Shimmerwine? It has a delicate flavor that is entirely unique to the vineyards of Eversong and it is the one thing I truly miss from my homeland.

Unfortunately, it is extremely hard to find on this side of the Thalassian Gate.

I had a patron bring me a bottle that he claimed to have "liberated" from blood elves in northern Azshara. If your adventures take you to that region and you can recover more bottles for me, I would handsomely reward your efforts.

entries.name: Thicker Than Water
entries.how:
Yes... yes, I will take the boy in. He is family and I'm all he has. I need to recover for a bit longer, but I'll be taking leave and heading to Dalaran as soon as I am able. 

Please return to the Matron and let her know that I am on my way. I'll do my best to ensure that my brother's child is kept safe and grows up strong.

I swear it.

entries.name: Special Access
entries.how:
Now that you've proven yourself as a stalwart and dependable ally, I've been authorized to teach you how to teleport yourself to our city.

We appreciate your service to Dalaran and the Kirin Tor. We hope to see you continue to grow in your mastery of magic.

entries.name: A Message in Blood
entries.how:
Does your blade thirst for human blood, {name}?

Some years ago, the human defectors laid claim to a small farm to the southwest across the river. With the area rich in lumber and stone, it was only a matter of time before they expanded their reach to the keep along the eastern shore known as Farholde.

Our first skirmishes would have ended in our favor if we'd had the numbers. It's time to remind them of our presence.

Disrupt their farming efforts. Take no prisoners. Send them a clear message.

entries.name: Food for the Taking
entries.how:
Humans within these lands have long enjoyed the warmth, comfort and sustenance these lands provide. It's time we start denying these humans such pleasantries.

Seek out the supplies of our enemies at the farm to the southwest. Take whatever you find.

It won't bring pleasure like bloodying a blade, but slowing them buys us time to plan our next move.

entries.name: Borrowed Blades
entries.how:
With the human presence to the south and Twilight to the west, the battle for resources has become difficult. But why gather resources amongst our enemies when their blades will suffice?

Follow the river south to the mill. When you hear the whistling of woodworkers among the trees, tread lightly. When the opportunity presents itself, strike hard and fast.

I'll stay behind to keep the forge running hot. Gur'dok will break down the blades while I fashion weaponry forged of their own materials.

entries.name: Farholde Scouting Report
entries.how: <The report is sealed with the sigil of Farholde. This information may be of interest to Krom'rosh at Rog'mar.>

entries.name: The Goblin Trader
entries.how:
While Gur'dok and I continue our work, we did fashion a particular blade for a friend--perhaps friend is too strong a word--for an acquaintance down at the docks. This particular individual is well known and connected all across the Kingdoms and beyond.

Take this. When you deliver it, let her know I sent you. And tell her we're even.

entries.name: A Gift From Our Enemies
entries.how:
The humans of these lands are only one of many threats. With the encroaching Twilight and snarls of gnolls echoing from the hills nearby, battle may call at a moment's notice. Maintaining the strength of our allies may be the difference between Rog'mar's success or our removal from these lands.

Deliver the goods you've gathered to Gorg. He'll make sure our allies are well fed.

entries.name: A Serving of Strength
entries.how:
This hearty stew keeps our trainees fed, enough so that our enemies remain at a distance.

Bring this and feed our trainees to the west. Don't listen to any complaints. With how difficult defending our supply lines has become, they should be so lucky we're not feeding them dirt.

entries.name: Show Them How It's Done
entries.how:
Our scouts have reported training camps by the river to the south. If I'd received word sooner, it would have saved us both the hassle of locating and removing the human filth in a timely manner.

Continue your efforts, {name}. Holding back the humans to their precious little keep will buy us time to focus on other matters at hand.

Be swift about it.

entries.name: Gnoll Infestation
entries.how:
Though the gnoll presence has dwindled with the Twilight's encroachment, the threat remains.

The hills to the southwest are infested with their kind, disrupting trades and travelers alike.

Clear a path for our allies by removing the threat.

entries.name: Snargl's Snout
entries.how:
Among the cackling inhabitants of the Bristle Hills southwest of here is an elder gnoll by the name of Snargl. The sounds emanating from this particular gnoll are quite unpleasant. Their presence inspires those around, creating a problem for allies and scouts who enter the area.

A trophy as a memento of our having dealt with this most unpleasant gnoll fiend would fit nicely with my collection.

Be swift about it, {name}.

entries.name: Bristle Hills Bandits
entries.how:
Our allies mining ore from the hills to the south reported several attacks by gnolls in the area.

Travel south, locate their camps and retrieve the stolen ore. Take it from their dead bodies if need be.

entries.name: Jom-jom's Escape
entries.how: Jom-jom came looking for friend. Now Jom-jom want to go home.

entries.name: My Kingdom for a Horse
entries.how:
Our warhorses come from two nearby farms. One of them, owned by the Wheeler family off the road just outside of town, has apparently lost all of their stock. The cause of this is currently unknown.

With no horses, we have no cavalry, and without cavalry, our campaign against the Horde stands no chance.

Thus, you see, this situation must be resolved with utmost haste. Of where to start, however, I am less sure.

Go to Wheeler's Grange and speak to Benjy. See what he has to say for himself.

entries.name: Freshwater Fiends
entries.how:
You seen those murlocs down by the river, just west of here? Nasty things. Bad for my animals, and bad for the wildlife. Not to mention, they've settled right on top of my favorite fishing spot!

There ain't a soul in the Riverglades who wouldn't appreciate you getting rid of a few, that's for sure. 

Please, kill any you see. You'd be doin' us a whole heap of good.

entries.name: Foal Play
entries.how:
I've got no idea what happened to our horses. I got up one morning to feed 'em and they were all gone, just like that.

Life outside Farholde's a bit rougher. Anything could've got 'em--animals, murlocs, orcs, you name it.

If we wanna narrow down our list of culprits, we oughta search around the stables for clues.

entries.name: Coyote Huntin'
entries.how:
There's a pack of coyotes livin' in a den west of here. We can see 'em sometimes from across the river. They used to hunt fish on the shore, but I guess the murlocs pushed 'em out of their usual feeding ground, and so they've taken to eating horses.

The leader of the coyote pack's a bigger one with dark fur. We'd nicknamed him "Sootfur". I reckon if you kill him, the rest'll scatter.

entries.name: Wheeler's Fleeing Steeds
entries.how:
From what you found, it seems like the coyotes got most of the horses. Still, there's a few not accounted for.

Those that didn't get eaten probably ran off scared someplace. I don't know how many of those horses there are, but we'd better find 'em before the coyotes come back.

<Benjy holds out a sack in front of you.>

Here. If you find one, give it some of our feed. That'll get it to trust you so you can lead it back here.

entries.name: Bloodmaster's Ring
entries.how:
You smashed weak Twilight ogres. But they weak.

Today you show Bloodmaster and little goblin friend you belong.

Tomorrow, maybe we meet again if you still breathing.

entries.name: Pay to Play
entries.how:
First things first. I'm gonna need a deposit for your, uh... safety.

Look, I don't make the rules here. It's required.

Now if you should choose not to pay I'll be forced to tell old Clugfist our new friend wasn't so keen on proving their strength to our warm, welcoming friends here.

That would be a real shame. Catch my drift, bub?

entries.name: Bloodmaster's Ring
entries.how:
The battle of the Bloodmaster's Ring begins!

We'll start you off easy here, pal. This flighty fiend'll take you down, then pick ya clean.

Now quit standin' around and step into the ring. Fame awaits!

entries.name: Encroaching Twilight
entries.how:
Humans are not our only adversary within the Riverglades, {name}, nor are they our most dire.

A cult known as the Twilight's Hammer has begun a campaign against those they deem heretics in the eyes of their twisted gods. The ravaged remains of a human settlement to the west are but the first to fall to their conquest. No doubt Rog'mar will be next.

We cannot afford to let them establish a foothold so close to our doorstep. Go to this so-called Sunnyglade and thin their numbers.

entries.name: Gnoll Infestation
entries.how:
The gnolls have been a thorn in our side ever since we arrived. While less a threat than the Twilight's Hammer, they are aggressive, persistent and, worst of all, numerous.

The hills beyond this post are infested with them, making passage to the north dangerous, and posing a threat to those living outside the walls of Farholde Keep.

If we are ever to make these lands safe, removing the gnoll threat is imperative.

entries.name: Snargl's Snout
entries.how:
Gnolls value strength above all else. By killing their strongest, we not only lessen the threat they pose physically, but also strike fear into their hearts.

In a den among the Bristle Hills is a notorious gnoll by the name of Snargl. His death would no doubt sow panic among the Redridge's ranks.

Bring me his snout, and be quick about it.

entries.name: Twilight Missives
entries.how:
There have always been small pockets of Twilight's Hammer cultists here and there, but never have I seen them in such numbers. They seem emboldened by someone, or something, to expand their influence.

I would know more of these cultists and what they seek. Their shadowmancers are blessed by the dark powers and are likely the most trusted within their order to lead attacks of this scale.

Bring me anything you find off their corpses that we may glean knowledge into their campaign.

entries.name: Digging for Answers
entries.how:
The Twilight's Hammer are here for more than simple chaos, {name}. They appear to be digging throughout the Riverglades for something. As for what they are searching for, I cannot say. A source of power, of course, but what that is still eludes me.

Their zealots may not be willing to divulge their secrets, but they must have someone doing the digging for them. These are the ones you are to question. Return to Sunnyglade and 'convince' one of their miners to talk. We must get to the bottom of this.

entries.name: Our Ogre Friend
entries.how:
Alright, so you won a few battles. I think you might have what it takes to make it here after all.

Before I convince our next combatant to jump into the ring with you there's something I need from you first--food for Chub'chob's pet boar, Snufflesnout.

I promised I'd look after it, and, well, this gig here's keepin' me quite busy. Trust me, this'll benefit the both of us.

Mosey on over to the east of Clugfist's clubhouse. You're lookin' for a shy fella who goes by the name Gobam.

entries.name: A Boar's Delight
entries.how:
Gobam know Chub'chob pet love to eat food. Specially good food!

Yum yum berry and plant from river make good treat for Snufflesnout. Berry sweet. Best berry from human farm near ocean.

You find. Bring back. Me help make big treat.

entries.name: A Treat for a Friend
entries.how:
Ok friend. Here is treat. Snufflesnout snort and be happy when she see this.

And tell goblin please stop talk so much.

entries.name: Bloodmaster's Ring
entries.how:
Glad you made it through the first round, I guess.

This next contestant and I go way back. He ain't the brightest fella, but he's sure good at pummeling anything in his path.

Just head on into the pit and get yourself ready while I make the announcement.

entries.name: The Wayward Warrior
entries.how:
You did well slowing the Twilight's Hammer. Their foothold in Sunnyglade has weakened and you've turned their ogre warriors against them. Now we take the fight to them.

My brother, Dag'rosh, has already gone ahead with a scouting party. I would have preferred he waited for you, but he is impulsive and overeager--like a true warrior. I'd be honored if you joined him in battle at their stronghold to the west.

entries.name: Carving a Path
entries.how:
Do you see the fortress just west of here? The Twilight's Shroud, they call it. Filled to the brim with Twilight's Hammer cowards.

They may have walls and numbers, but their pitiful reliance on devilry and ancient gods makes them weak. Show them how vulnerable they really are!

entries.name: Break Their Chains
entries.how:
Those Twilight's Hammer dogs caught us before we could properly begin our attack. I was able to fight my way out, but my warriors were not so lucky. They were dragged off by the cult's champions and imprisoned in the fortress to the west.

Orcs do not belong in cages, {class}. Free my brothers and sisters, and we will show these mongrels a real fight.

entries.name: Bring Me His Head
entries.how:
Tran'gul's notes pointed to a leader of this Twilight's Hammer presence somewhere in that fortress. With my warriors free and the cult's numbers in disarray, now is the time to pierce the heart of this infestation.

Return to the Twilight's Shroud and enter their Stronghold. That is where you will find Overlord Kilgar. That is where we will exact our revenge.

entries.name: What We Lost
entries.how:
If you've come to demand more of our crop, you're too late. No doubt you saw my farm. Destroyed. All of it.

Good folk toiled in these fields for years to feed troops and civilians alike. But when those cultists arrived, where was the military? Where was our promised protection after all the rations they'd taken from us?

If you've any sense of decency, I beg you. The least we can do is recover their belongings from those cursed raiders. Let my people rest with their kin in the graveyard to the west.

entries.name: Belle's Ring
entries.how:
Unfortunately I haven't had much luck with identifying the ring's owner to bring closure to their family.

Perhaps Daythor can be of assistance. He knew the others of our regiment quite well.

I only hope it does not bring back unpleasant memories...

entries.name: Unsavory Plant Food
entries.how:
We make our own fertilizer out here. It's a special formula of mine that reeks like hell, but grows trees like they're weeds.

It's a 1:1:2 ratio of crawfish shells, manure, and murloc heads. Tasty, right?

The manure's easy enough. We've got the ranch to the south for that. The heads and shells? Those you're going to have to go wading in the river for.

If you feel like lending a hand, we could sure use your help getting some fertilizer ingredients.

entries.name: From Seed to Sprout
entries.how:
Considering you got yourself wrist-deep in guts and manure for us, it's only right you get to do the fun part too.

The boys and I gather seeds from the trees as we work. With the fertilizer you've provided, I've made a planting kit to put them in the ground to grow new saplings.

Take it, and find some good planting spots around the work sites.

entries.name: If a Tree Falls, and No One Hears...
entries.how:
Stranger, listen to me!

I work as a lumberjack for the nearby logging camp. As you can see, I've been trapped here in an accident. If I don't get out from here soon, I'll either bleed out, or be eaten by wild animals.

Please, go to the logging camp and fetch help!

entries.name: All That's Left
entries.how:
There was one more thing I wanted to talk to you about, friend.

When the Twilight's Hammer attacked, I put everyone who couldn't defend themselves in the barn to hide. I thought they would be safe. I thought...

<Elbrim's voice cracks as he recounts what happened.>

If you could do me one last kindness, will you go see what's left of my family? They should be buried here at home with me. I just don't have the heart to check myself.

entries.name: Helping Hands
entries.how:
Well, I guess that explains why Curly didn't come back for lunch break. Looks like I have to bail him out again -- typical. The way he makes me worry, I swear, I'll be gray in a year.

Come on, we'll have to save him ourselves, and it sounds like we don't have much time.

entries.name: Saving Sunnyglade
entries.how:
When you look around you, what do you see? A broken home and a tired people.

Stormwind has left us to fend for ourselves, and we have less to do that with every day. Many within these walls are refugees who barely escaped tragedy without so much as even their own families.

Farholde is no Stormwind, stranger. We lost a settlement in the northwest to the Twilight's Hammer, but we will not let them keep it. If you wish to fight, go to Sunnyglade and purge those savages from our lands.

entries.name: Scraps of Knowledge
entries.how:
You've seen the ruined city to the north, yes? Sunnyglade? Demar tries sending troops, but we're no closer to reclaiming it. I have a better idea.

In truth, this attack by the Twilight's Hammer is not the first. They seem to be coordinating from a centralized location, and I would know where.
